stories.headline: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Players to watch, buzz and goals for all 32 teams
stories.summary: We outlined deadline plans for all 32 teams, including who could be dealt before 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Here's what you need to know.
stories.byline: NFL Nation, Jeremy Fowler, Dan Graziano, Aaron Schatz and Seth Walder
stories.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. We have already had a fair share of trades made this season, but could more be on the horizon? Will the Colts continue to trade players away -- such as Jonathan Taylor -- and build draft capital for the future? Will the Chiefs finally find a trade for a dependable wide receiver for QB Patrick Mahomes? How will the Eagles and Ravens approach things without their QB1s? Let's take a 32-team look at what to expect over the next week.

First, we checked where each team stands through Week 8 using ESPN's Football Power Index projections. Then, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to name each team's trade deadline goal. Who is staying put, and who is open for business? Next, NFL insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano leaned on their reporting to predict which players on every team could be on the move. Finally, analysts Aaron Schatz and Seth Walder picked one player each team should try to acquire.

Here's everything you need to know heading into the deadline.

Jump to:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

Arizona Cardinals (3-5)
Chance to make playoffs: 1.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 8

What is the deadline goal? Keep building for the future. That seems to be the M.O. of another M.O. -- Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort. He's in Year 4 of a three-year rebuild that hasn't blossomed yet. Moving players who are unhappy or veterans for draft capital is not out of the question after trading Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans last month. The Cardinals want to build toward the future, especially for next season when they will likely have to address the quarterback position again. -- Josh Weinfuss

Who could be on the move? Edge Josh Sweat. The Cardinals have received trade interest on Sweat, who would be a natural fit in Dallas. Word is he wants a new deal, which could be a hurdle. Safety Budda Baker and quarterback Jacoby Brissett are also names to watch. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Vikings WR Tai Felton. Felton has only six receptions in a season and a half in the NFL, but the Cardinals could try to find the skills that made him a third-round pick in 2025. They need young receiving talent behind Michael Wilson. -- Schatz

Atlanta Falcons (3-5)
Chance to make playoffs: 7.9%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 10

What is the deadline goal? Don't give up valuable future assets. New Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham hated that the team had only five draft picks in 2026. He vowed that the franchise would never have that few again. Cunningham wants to build the Falcons through the draft. So, do not expect him to gamble away picks unless there's a no-brainer offer out there. The Falcons are unlikely to be active with their 3-5 record, because they still believe they can win the NFC South. They just won't give up important draft capital to do it. -- Marc Raimondi

Who could be on the move? Safety Jessie Bates III. To be clear ... I do not believe the Falcons are trying to trade Bates, and I would be surprised if they did. But he's an excellent player in the final year of his contract, and there are teams out there that would like to know whether they can get him. I believe it would take a huge offer. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Texans WR Kayshon Boutte. This would be the second time Boutte has been traded this season, after the Patriots dealt him to Houston in August. But that was before the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr. (and before the Texans got out to a 2-5 start). The Falcons are 3-5 but not out of the race in the NFC South, so adding a cheap player who could help is not out of the question, and Boutte is exactly that. -- Walder

Baltimore Ravens (4-4)
Chance to make playoffs: 7.2%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 11

What is the deadline goal? Trade for a QB or listen to offers. With injured QB Lamar Jackson (right thumb) out for at least four games and perhaps the season, the Ravens have to decide whether they want to add a quarterback to try to keep the season afloat or trade their own players for capital. Running back Derrick Henry could be a target for a championship contender. But it wouldn't be surprising if the Ravens stand pat. -- Jamison Hensley

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Rashod Bateman. Several teams are looking for receiver help, and Bateman would have value, should Baltimore entertain it. He's not a focal point in the offense and would probably welcome the chance to be more of one elsewhere. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett. The injury to Jackson completely changes the Ravens' needs. They're still in the playoff race and need a quarterback with more experience than undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. Brissett might have lost his job to Gardner Minshew II on Sunday, but he still ranks 24th among qualified quarterbacks with a 48.9 QBR. That's not good, but that's not undrafted rookie level, either. -- Schatz

Buffalo Bills (6-1)
Chance to make playoffs: 99.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 31

What is the deadline goal? Be aggressive with secondary options. With the way the Bills' offense is playing, a league-average defense should be enough to make them serious contenders. Now, the salary cap situation complicates things. With the roster as is, the Bills have a little less than $4 million to spend. But they should be in the market for an extra safety or nickel corner to fortify a weakness and alleviate some of the concerns caused by injuries and early-season mistakes. -- Nick Suss

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Keon Coleman. Coleman has played well enough to stay in Buffalo's short-term and maybe long-term plans. But I'm not sure this team will trade anyone. So consider this pure speculation that Coleman could be attractive enough to a receiver-needy team to bring back the defensive help Buffalo seeks. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Buccaneers edge Yaya Diaby. He would provide a jolt of pass rush to a defense that badly needs it. Buffalo ranks 26th in pass rush win rate, but Diaby's win rate at edge is in the 97th percentile this season, and he has 3.0 sacks. The Bills are in a tight cap situation, but Diaby is a pending free agent. -- Walder

Carolina Panthers (3-4)
Chance to make playoffs: 23.6%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 13

What is the deadline goal? Find cost-effective help, if possible. The Panthers are in an awkward spot after losing two consecutive games and firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. But while they are under .500, they're still leading the NFC South entering Week 9. Carolina needs help at cornerback and on the offensive line. Coach Dave Canales said they're open to improving the roster with a trade, but they'll need to use some salary cap gymnastics (they have less than $1 million in cap space) to make that happen. -- Mike Kaye

Who could be on the move? Tight end Ja'Tavion Sanders. Sanders has fallen out of favor in Carolina and was a healthy scratch Thursday night in Green Bay. Sanders doesn't hold significant value, but perhaps a Day 3 pick swap gets this done. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Jets S Andre Cisco. This goes with the recommendation for the Jets, a suggestion that New York send a veteran free safety to the contending Panthers in exchange for youth at the position. This would also allow sixth-round rookie Zakee Wheatley more time to develop and improve the Panthers' pass defense, which ranks 21st in DVOA against deep passes. -- Schatz

Chicago Bears (6-2)
Chance to make playoffs: 90.4%

Projected first-round draft slot: No pick

What is the deadline goal? All-in. The Bears showed they are trying to win a Super Bowl when they sent two first-round picks and a fourth to the Tennessee Titans for All-Pro DT Jeffery Simmons (and a fifth) on Oct. 29. Chicago took on the remaining $7.9 million of Simmons' 2026 compensation, which is his cap charge for the rest of the season. The leaves the team with just under $4 million in available cap space, according to Roster Management System, which provides some flexibility if the Bears want to keep adding. Bolstering their group of edge rushers might not cost the Bears more than a Day 3 pick. -- Courtney Cronin

Who could be on the move? Quarterback Case Keenum. This is another team that I don't think would be moving players. But teams always need QB help, and Keenum showed a little something earlier this season in relief of Caleb Williams. For the right offer, who knows? -- Graziano

Who should they target? Dolphins edge Josh Uche. The Bears already paid a ton to bring in Simmons, so I assume they'll be seeking bargains for the rest of deadline season. But they still could use some help at edge, and Uche could contribute to that rotation alongside Montez Sweat, Austin Booker and Daniel Hardy. This season, Uche has recorded a pass rush win rate that ranks in the 60th percentile and a pressure rate in the 35th percentile at edge. -- Walder

Cincinnati Bengals (5-2)
Chance to make playoffs: 96.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 28

What is the deadline goal? Potentially landing depth at linebacker or cornerback. Those position groups have needed to be fortified dating back to last offseason. The Bengals are off to their best start since 2021, the season they reached the Super Bowl, so they could look to improve. They have the salary cap space ($7.4 million) to make a small move to address needs. -- Ben Baby

Who could be on the move? Edge Shemar Stewart. Coach Zac Taylor has poured cold water on this, saying any talk of a Stewart trade is "made up." But he's not playing much right now, and teams have him on their radar just in case. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Saints LB Pete Werner. A 27-year-old linebacker right in his prime, Werner would help improve the Bengals' defense up the middle. He's good on blitzes and against the run. Last season, he had a 70% run stop rate -- meaning that 70% of his run tackles stopped the runner short of a successful play. -- Schatz

Cleveland Browns (5-3)
Chance to make playoffs: 17.3%

Projected first-round draft slot: Nos. 15, 19

What is the deadline goal? Supplement the young core. The Browns are ahead of schedule with the second-youngest team in the NFL and have the draft capital -- 11 selections in the 2027 draft -- to make a big swing. But with ongoing quarterback questions, it might be best to maintain their picks. GM Andrew Berry is always open to swinging a trade, but a less flashy move to add depth, namely at tight end or defensive line, seems more realistic. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy. He has made some plays, and Cleveland could certainly keep him around. But the team is going much younger at receiver, so it makes sense to listen if teams are into Jeudy, who is still somehow only 27 years old. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Raiders QB Kirk Cousins. The Browns are in an unexpectedly strong position with an actual chance to make the playoffs. The talk of Deshaun Watson's improved play has been vastly overstated, as he ranks 28th in QBR. Cousins is playing much better (16th in QBR) and would likely get more out of the surging young playmakers. He would be a temporary solution at quarterback, but that's better than trying to get to the postseason with Watson at QB. -- Walder

Dallas Cowboys (3-5)
Chance to make playoffs: 43.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 21

What is the deadline goal? The Cowboys could be all over the map. Owner Jerry Jones has said he would be willing to make a trade to help this team, but given the start to the season, would a trade for a pass rusher really change the dynamics on defense? Dallas has only four picks in 2027, so assets are low. The Cowboys made a big move already in acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers. While he has played well when on the field, an ankle injury has nagged him. The biggest decision they have to make is whether George Pickens is part of their future. If he isn't, would it be wiser to acquire more picks than potentially waiting for a 2028 compensatory pick if he leaves in free agency? -- Todd Archer

Who could be on the move? Tight end Luke Schoonmaker. There are a lot of directions Dallas could go here. But the struggling defense can't afford to move players on that side of the ball. Schoonmaker is No. 3 tight end in the pecking order, and teams are looking for blocking tight ends. I just don't see Dallas moving key players at this point. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Jets edge Kingsley Enagbare. The Cowboys are currently 31st in pass rush win rate and still need help on the edge. The 26-year-old Enagbare is having a career season, ranked eighth among edges in pass rush win rate, and he's on a one-year deal. As an added bonus, Enagbare is also third among edges in run stop win rate. -- Schatz

Denver Broncos (6-2)
Chance to make playoffs: 93.9%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 27

What is the deadline goal? Finding the balance between what they want now and what they'll need later. The Broncos have a long list of free agents come March, including three starters in the league's deepest secondary. They have picked just twice in the first round of the past five drafts and didn't pick until the third round last April. So, any desires about a running back or other skill positions in an offense that has been a teeth-grinding affair to this point have to go beyond a short-term option. -- Jeff Legwold

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. Mims is very young (24), and the Broncos likely aren't interested in moving him. But he's in the final year of his contract and has speed and the ability to help in the return game. Teams like young guys who can do multiple things. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Eagles G Landon Dickerson. One of the reasons quarterback Bo Nix had early career success was because he played behind one of the best offensive lines. This season, that hasn't been the case with the Broncos ranking 20th in pass block win rate. Dickerson is not a guarantee after his performance fell off last season and a knee injury cost him a slew of games this season. But he doesn't have guaranteed money after 2026. The Broncos can be the team that rolls the dice on him returning to form. -- Walder

Detroit Lions (5-2)
Chance to make playoffs: 78.3%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 24

What is the deadline goal? Adding help to the secondary. Lions GM Brad Holmes looks at everything, according to head coach Dan Campbell. "I mean, he's nonstop," Campbell said Oct. 30. Earlier this season, the coach acknowledged that the Lions were engaged in trade talks for corner Joey Porter Jr. (who ended up in Dallas), as they desired to add help to the unit. Detroit's defense could still benefit from an experienced cornerback, and the draft capital is there to help, as the Lions are projected to have 10 picks in 2027. -- Eric Woodyard

Who could be on the move? Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. The Lions don't have any obvious trade candidates, but Rakestraw, a 2024 second-round pick, was benched in Week 8. The Lions have depth issues in the defensive backfield, though, so this might be a nonstarter. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Dolphins CB JuJu Brents. The Lions' secondary is helped immensely by getting safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch back from injury, but they could still use another cornerback. Brents becomes a free agent at the end of this season and has been surprisingly effective for the Dolphins, ranking third among qualifying cornerbacks in my coverage DVOA metric behind Trent McDuffie and Jahdae Barron. -- Schatz

Green Bay Packers (5-3)
Chance to make playoffs: 49.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No pick

What is the deadline goal? Help the running game. The Packers are very much in the NFC playoff picture despite having the worst running game in the NFL. At 60.6 rushing yards per game, they're nearly 17 yards behind the next-worse running team, the Raiders. The Packers appear to be in the mix for running back Jonathan Taylor if the Colts move him, despite not having a 2027 first-round pick. But given how bad their blocking has been, an offensive lineman or two might make more sense than a running back. -- Rob Demovsky

Who could be on the move? Cornerback Keisean Nixon. Nixon is another player in the final year of his deal who has return-game chops. The Packers need a lot of help with OL and RB, and maybe dangling a player from the current roster could help. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Colts K Spencer Shrader. The biggest issue for Green Bay this season has been its offensive line. But the most easily fixed problem might be at kicker, with sixth-round rookie Trey Smack struggling. Actually, that's putting it mildly. Smack has recorded minus-2.1 field goals over expected, second worst in the NFL this season, along with three missed PATs. Shrader is on the other end of that spectrum, with 4.1 field goals made over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. He's in a contract year, too. -- Walder

Houston Texans (2-5)
Chance to make playoffs: 25.7%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 16

What is the deadline goal? Keep assets. Houston isn't in the position to trade players away. It wants to stay competitive in hopes of clawing back into the playoff hunt. The Texans have already given up a 2027 second-round pick for wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. to bolster the receiving room. If the season goes south, they'll need all six 2027 draft picks to revamp the roster. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Who could be on the move? Edge Jadeveon Clowney. Clowney has generated trade interest, and because he has played for seven NFL teams over his 13-year career, he's comfortable with gun-for-hire status. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Raiders CB Taron Johnson. The Texans could use more depth at the nickel with Jalen Pitre dealing with a left shoulder injury. When Pitre returns, having the veteran Johnson around would allow Pitre to occasionally spell Reed Blankenship at safety (or even start in his place). -- Schatz

Indianapolis Colts (2-6)
Chance to make playoffs: 1.7%

Projected first-round draft slot: No pick

What is the deadline goal? Prepare for the future. The Colts told the league what they think about their prospects for this season when they traded stars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week. And they are still fielding lots of calls, especially for Taylor, who has two years remaining on his contract and is still among the NFL's elite backs. Receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade, and there is a non-zero chance that nose tackle Grover Stewart is moved. -- Stephen Holder

Who could be on the move? Running back Jonathan Taylor. We could have put a half-dozen names here easily, but this one is the most fun. It's going to take a big offer to get the Colts to deal away the 27-year-old Taylor with two years left on his contract, but teams are exploring it. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Cardinals DL Darius Robinson. There aren't many players who make sense for the Colts to add, but a young player whose value has dropped could be an option if the Colts want to take a shot at developing them. Robinson has played only 36% of the Cardinals' defensive snaps this season but is showing signs of life in pass rush. Robinson has a 16% pass rush win rate when playing defensive tackle, which is roughly average, and a 13% pressure rate as an interior rusher, which is well above average. -- Walder

Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2)
Chance to make playoffs: 97.8%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 30

What is the deadline goal? Help on the interior of the defensive line was a need before Sunday's game, and it's even more so after the right knee injury to nose tackle DaVon Hamilton. Hamilton was the key to the Jaguars' top-ranked run defense, and now they will be looking for a replacement run-stuffer as well as trying to find someone who can help provide interior pass rush, a lack of which has been a problem. The Jaguars have only $4.6 million in cap space, so that might make it a little harder for GM James Gladstone to maneuver. -- Mike DiRocco

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. The Jaguars have been unwilling to explore trading him just yet. But several team execs believe the significant trade interest in Thomas and his declining role in Jacksonville will eventually facilitate a deal, with the likes of Kansas City and Pittsburgh in the market. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Raiders G Spencer Burford. Pass blocking is one of the Jaguars' few weaknesses this season, and right guard Ezra Cleveland's 78.7% pass block win rate ranks 63rd out of 66 qualifying guards. Burford is on a one-year contract in Las Vegas, and his pass block win rate is 90.5%, which ranks 10th. -- Schatz

Kansas City Chiefs (5-2)
Chance to make playoffs: 90.9%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 26

What is the deadline goal? Get a receiver. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Chiefs are looking for a receiver, which makes sense because it's clear QB Patrick Mahomes needs a receiver to depend on. In the loss to the Seahawks, the Chiefs' receivers combined for six receptions for 39 yards. Even with Rashee Rice (seven receptions for 53 yards and a touchdown) back in the lineup against the Broncos, the rest of the group generated just six receptions for 37 yards. The Chiefs also have two 2027 third-round picks at their disposal. -- Nate Taylor

Who could be on the move? Cornerback Kristian Fulton. He's in the final year of his contract and making almost $10 million this season. The Chiefs could free up some money with a move like this to bring in help for their lackluster offense. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Buccaneers WR Chris Godwin Jr. In Godwin, the Chiefs would get a veteran player who is past his prime -- just 1.2 yards per route run this season -- but could still be an asset. Godwin is playing on a fully guaranteed $22 million salary, so this trade would involve the Bucs converting almost all of Godwin's remaining money into a signing bonus before dealing him in exchange for a draft pick. Tampa Bay would be unlikely to keep Godwin on his current contract in 2027, so if they believe they are out of contention this season, it could make sense to get something for him now. -- Walder

Las Vegas Raiders (4-4)
Chance to make playoffs: 9.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 12

What is the deadline goal? Stand pat and continue to evaluate the roster. The Raiders do not plan to trade star defensive end Maxx Crosby, who wants to remain in Las Vegas. With that said, Las Vegas is better off standing pat and evaluating the current talent on the roster. The Raiders don't have a ton of players outside of Crosby who could give them significant value in return. Sure, Las Vegas could trade for a wide receiver or maybe an interior defensive lineman. But if that move requires them to part ways with a substantial amount of draft capital, they shouldn't do so. -- Ryan McFadden

Who could be on the move? Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson. Powers-Johnson fell out of the Raiders' offensive line rotation, and though the Raiders are not actively seeking to trade him, the expectation is they would listen to offers. Teams always need offensive line help. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. The Raiders have thrown only 41% of passes to wide receivers. That's the lowest figure in the NFL. The Jaguars have pretty much given up on Thomas, but he would become the clear No. 1 option in Las Vegas, and perhaps he could find the form that helped him catch 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie in 2024. -- Schatz

Los Angeles Chargers (0-7)
Chance to make playoffs: 0.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 3

What is the deadline goal? Look for ways to build for future. The winless Chargers might be thinking about potential coaching and general manager changes and could choose to initiate a roster teardown and rebuild. Los Angeles should at least look to move older players who are not in the team's long-term plans for contention. -- Ben Solak

Who could be on the move? Edge Khalil Mack. He is making $8 million this year, so the acquiring team would be on the hook for only about half of that. Let's get Mack someplace where he can get to a Super Bowl before all is said and done. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Raiders OL Jackson Powers-Johnson. The only acquisition the Chargers should be making is one aimed at the future, and they've struggled to find reliable play in the interior of their offensive line for years. Powers-Johnson was recently benched, and the Chargers could take a stab at developing him in hopes of realizing the potential that made him a second-round pick in 2024. Powers-Johnson is under contract through 2027. -- Walder

Los Angeles Rams (4-4)
Chance to make playoffs: 44%

Projected first-round draft slot: No pick

What is the deadline goal? Stay put. The Rams have only four draft picks in 2027 (their own second-, fourth-, fifth- and sixth-rounders). Coach Sean McVay said the team doesn't plan to add externally before the deadline, as others in the division have. Instead, the Rams view the players they'll be getting back from injury in the next month as their additions. "Maybe it'd be a different conversation if we're talking about guys that are on IR and done for the whole season," McVay said. -- Sarah Barshop

Who could be on the move? Cornerback Emmanuel Forbes Jr. He lost his starting spot to additions Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, and perhaps he has untapped ability as a rangy 2023 first-round pick who has shown glimpses in Los Angeles. The Lions are among teams looking for corner help. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Commanders WR Dyami Brown. Brown is on a one-year deal; he would give the Rams a veteran field stretcher who could play some snaps while Davante Adams (hamstring) is out, and as an added bonus, he's lauded as a run blocker. McVay loves wide receivers who can run block. -- Schatz

Miami Dolphins (1-6)
Chance to make playoffs: Projected first-round draft slot: No. 2

What is the deadline goal? Keeping the team leaders. The Dolphins aren't looking to acquire players at the deadline, and their record might lead some to believe they could be looking to trade their own. Miami's most logical trade candidates (RT Austin Jackson and DT Zach Sieler) are critical among their position groups -- especially Sieler. But if a big offer comes, GM Jon-Eric Sullivan proved with the Jaylen Waddle trade that he isn't afraid to deal a valued player. The focus moving forward is to get better, not just accumulate draft capital. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Who could be on the move? Edge Josh Uche. Uche is a productive player on a super-cheap contract who could help as part of a contender's pass rush rotation. If he's not part of Miami's plans beyond this season, why not get something for him? -- Graziano

Who should they target? Texans OT Braden Smith. It doesn't usually make sense for a team in Miami's position to acquire veterans, but one exception is trying to improve pass protection to aid in quarterback development. Smith might be an upgrade at right tackle for the Dolphins: Jackson's pass block win rate ranks in the 12th percentile, and Smith ranked in the 46th percentile last season with the Colts. And $2.5 million of Smith's $8 million 2027 salary is fully guaranteed. -- Walder

Minnesota Vikings (6-1)
Chance to make playoffs: 83.9%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 25

What is the deadline goal? Careful decisions. The Vikings understand their winning start has put them in strong position for a playoff spot, if not an NFC North title. Their winning formula -- elite-level defense and special teams, with an offense that doesn't commit many turnovers -- has been used by many Super Bowl teams. But they also want to preserve their future draft classes for new GM Nolan Teasley, who was hired in part to restock the roster with young talent. So they will and have listened to every possibility and are interested in adding to both lines as well as at running back and tight end but will make careful decisions. -- Kevin Seifert

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Jauan Jennings. The Vikings had trade talks with San Francisco about Jennings, who preferred to stay in Minnesota, and the team obliged. And he has played 62 snaps over the past two weeks, so perhaps both sides can move forward. But he has been in trade discussions already, so he can always return to the conversation. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Chargers QB Justin Herbert. Go big or go home. Would coach Kevin O'Connell be able to unlock the skills that made Herbert great early in his career in a way coordinator Mike McDaniel hasn't been able to? -- Schatz

New England Patriots (5-3)
Chance to make playoffs: 80.8%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 23

What is the deadline goal? Play the field. If that means capitalizing on the availability of a modest-salaried player who might help address a depth-based need such as at defensive tackle or outside linebacker, the Patriots should pounce. If that means another team might be willing to part with a significant future asset for a high-salaried player whose loss could be absorbed, they should pounce on that as well. The Patriots have less than $5 million is salary cap space and are projected to have nine draft picks in 2027. -- Mike Reiss

Who could be on the move? Quarterback Tommy DeVito. I don't think the Patriots are trading players. However, DeVito is a backup quarterback with NFL starting experience, so it's not crazy to think New England could get a call. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Saints G Cesar Ruiz. Both of the Patriots' Week 1 starters at guard -- Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Mike Onwenu (ankle) -- are on injured reserve. In Ruiz, New England would be adding a starting-caliber guard who is having a particularly good season, with a 78th percentile pass block win rate. He's a better pass protector than run blocker, but the former is more important in New England where protecting Drake Maye is the most important job of the offensive line. -- Walder

New Orleans Saints (2-5)
Chance to make playoffs: 7.2%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 7

What is the deadline goal? Get what they can. The Saints aren't going to gain a lot of cap space from any trade because they restructured all of their major contracts, but now would be the time to see whether any of their older veterans who likely won't be on the team in 2027 or younger players who aren't contributing much could be sent to another team for a short-term gain. The Saints are struggling in enough areas that trying to acquire players at the trade deadline isn't likely to make a major difference in their performance. -- Katherine Terrell

Who could be on the move? Safety Justin Reid. Multiple teams could use safety help, from Buffalo to Jacksonville. Reid is 29 and has 124 career starts. He's due $9.3 million this season, and his guarantees run out in 2027. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw. The Saints are last in the NFL in run defense DVOA, and the veteran Kinlaw ranks 22nd among interior defensive linemen with a 34.4% run stop win rate. -- Schatz

New York Giants (4-2-1)
Chance to make playoffs: 47.3%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 17

What is the deadline goal? Bring in reinforcements for this season and beyond. That is the key. GM Joe Schoen said any move would have to be for the "short term and long term." Two positions to monitor closely are running back and defensive line. The Giants have already shown significant interest in Colts running back Jonathan Taylor with the NFC East title clearly in the picture. -- Jordan Raanan

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Darnell Mooney. Mooney is a veteran wide receiver who doesn't make much money on a team with a potentially emerging rookie receiver in Malachi Fields. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Falcons DT Maason Smith. The Falcons are suddenly somewhat loaded at defensive tackle. The stats paint a bit of a mixed picture on Smith, who ranks in the 96th percentile in pass rush win rate and 38th percentile in pressure rate. But the Giants could use an interior player who could provide some pass rushing threat in passing situations, and Smith could be that. -- Walder

New York Jets (2-6)
Chance to make playoffs: 0.3%

Projected first-round draft slot: Nos. 5, 6, 14

What is the deadline goal? Keep an eye on the future. The goal is to keep building for the long term -- a mission that began in earnest last season with the Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams trades. The Jets don't expect to be particularly active, but they will examine potential deals that fetch a draft pick or a player who can help in 2027. Their most immediate need is defensive tackle, a position hurt by injuries. Despite rumors, the Jets reportedly have no plans to trade receiver Garrett Wilson or running back Breece Hall. -- Rich Cimini

Who could be on the move? Edge Will McDonald IV. I was told the Jets do not plan to trade McDonald. But he's more of a complementary player in the Jets' edge rush rotation when everyone is healthy, and if pass-rush-needy teams strike out elsewhere, perhaps they make an attractive offer to the Jets. Hall was tempting to list here, as was corner Nahshon Wright. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Panthers S Lathan Ransom. Ransom was in line to be a starting safety this season but has been passed in the lineup by rookie Zakee Wheatley. The 2025 fourth-round pick would add to a Jets defensive backfield that could lose veterans Dane Belton and Andre Cisco to free agency in 2027. -- Schatz

Philadelphia Eagles (2-6)
Chance to make playoffs: 0.8%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 4

What is the deadline goal? Philly wants to retool on the fly. We have already seen the front office's willingness to move on from players when it sent center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens in early October. The Eagles have fallen further out of contention since, increasing the chances GM Howie Roseman would be willing to part with others not in the team's long-term plans if the compensation is right. Given the lack of appetite for a complete rebuild in Philadelphia, a high volume of trades is unlikely, but it would not be a surprise if Roseman makes a couple of moves as the Eagles continue to stockpile picks for the 2027 and '28 drafts. -- Tim McManus

Who could be on the move? Cornerback Riq Woolen. Woolen was a part of a Super Bowl champion team just nine months ago. The Eagles' season seems to have gone down the drain, and I would expect moves in both directions. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Jets RB Isaiah Davis. Even if the Eagles aren't going to trade running back Saquon Barkley before the trade deadline (and I think they should), they could use some depth behind him. In Davis, the Eagles would get a player who is the Jets' third running back but has shown some promise: He has posted 1.0 rush yards over expected per carry over his career, per NFL Next Gen Stats. If the Eagles are going to play out an uncompetitive season, they might as well play some young players and find out whether they can offer value going forward. -- Walder

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2)
Chance to make playoffs: 80%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 22

What is the deadline goal? Don't mortgage the future for the present. Coming off their most well-rounded performance, the Steelers aren't in desperation mode at the trade deadline. They could use help at cornerback and wide receiver, but only if the price is right. While the Steelers are in win-now mode, their top priority remains finding their next franchise quarterback. While that answer could be on the roster in Drew Allar or Will Howard, the Steelers still don't want to surrender the kind of significant draft capital that could be used to land a premium prospect. -- Brooke Pryor

Who could be on the move? Quarterback Mason Rudolph. The Steelers are more likely to bring in players at the deadline. In fact, I don't expect Pittsburgh to move anyone. But it has a surplus at quarterback, and should more quarterback injuries occur around the league, perhaps teams call on Rudolph with an attractive offer. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Colts WR Josh Downs. The Colts and Steelers already made a deal for one wide receiver in the offseason, so why not another one? Downs' ability to get open against zone coverage would fit the short passing game the Steelers run with Aaron Rodgers. -- Schatz

San Francisco 49ers (6-1)
Chance to make playoffs: 99.1%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 32

What is the deadline goal? Go for it. The 49ers have been hearing for years that their Super Bowl window is closing, yet they remain in the mix. This season, the Niners established it early with a winning start, but injuries along the defensive line and at receiver have made their needs obvious. They already acquired DT DeForest Buckner, but it would be a surprise if San Francisco didn't, as OT Trent Williams told ESPN, "go for broke" with another meaningful addition (or two). -- Nick Wagoner

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. Be honest. You forgot he was still there, right? A ton of issues would need to be worked out, but it's hard to imagine he just never plays again -- especially because he just hired an agent. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Jets WR Adonai Mitchell. It's no secret that the 49ers are down bad at wide receiver. Mitchell has long flashed more promise than results, though we saw that promise Sunday when he recorded seven receptions for 142 yards and a touchdown. The Jets might be reluctant to part with Mitchell. But because they have Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr. and Kenyon Sadiq, it's worth making a call. -- Walder

Seattle Seahawks (4-4)
Chance to make playoffs: 48%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 20

What is the deadline goal? Be ready to strike if the right deal is available. There aren't any glaring holes on the Seahawks' roster, which already got one boost last week with the trade for left guard Quenton Nelson. Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to Seattle's backfield as well. But depending on the severity of some recent injuries -- wide receiver Rashid Shaheed and outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu missed Week 8 -- a few spots could use a reinforcement. Even after giving up a 2027 third-round pick (and a 2028 fifth-rounder) for Nelson, the Seahawks are projected to have 10 selections in next year's draft. -- Brady Henderson

Who could be on the move? Guard Anthony Bradford. Bradford is the odd man out after the Nelson acquisition, and though parting with guard depth would be tough for the contending Seahawks, Bradford could net GM John Schneider an extra draft pick. -- Fowler

Who should they target? Colts TE Mo Alie-Cox. The Seahawks use multiple tight ends on roughly 40% of snaps but lost Elijah Arroyo to a season-ending shoulder injury. Alie-Cox, who is on a one-year contract, is a block-first tight end who can alternate with Eric Saubert and help improve the Seahawks' running game. -- Schatz

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5)
Chance to make playoffs: 64.6%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 18

What is the deadline goal? Two straight dominant wins have pulled the Bucs out of expected fire sale mode ahead of the trade deadline, and they now appear more likely to stand pat and lean on their veteran roster in a tight NFC South race. Multiple teams have inquired about star defensive tackle Vita Vea this year, per sources, but the Bucs have been reluctant to deal him. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also seen as a trade target, but his Grade 2 MCL sprain might complicate those pursuits. -- Cameron Wolfe

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. The Buccaneers haven't completed a pass in their past 15 drives, and they've won their past two games. If you don't ever need to throw it, what are you doing with all of these wide receivers? -- Graziano

Who should they target? Eagles TE Dallas Goedert. The Buccaneers brought back Cade Otton on a three-year deal, but thus far the results have been disappointing. Otton has managed just 0.9 yards per route run, and his blocking numbers are down, with a run block win rate in just the 19th percentile. Goedert isn't going to help in the latter area, but he will in the former: He has recorded 1.8 yards per route run. -- Walder

Tennessee Titans (1-7)
Chance to make playoffs: Projected first-round draft slot: Nos. 1, 29

What is the deadline goal? Continue to evaluate the roster. Trading their best player, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, for two first-round picks made a big splash. Coach Robert Saleh and GM Mike Borgonzi said the deal was one they couldn't pass up and a trade that will accelerate their rebuild process. But the Titans need to figure out who will be part of the rebuild, starting with quarterback Cam Ward. Tennessee has some additional players who could garner decent value in running back Tony Pollard, safety Amani Hooker and wide receiver Calvin Ridley. But Borgonzi said he doesn't intend to make more moves, at least not unless he gets another offer he can't refuse. -- Turron Davenport

Who could be on the move? Wide receiver Calvin Ridley. Ridley is considered a backup plan for a few teams in the receiver market. The sense I get from talking to teams is the Titans would need a quality Day 3 pick to part with Ridley, whose $13 million in 2026 cash could be a hurdle based on his low production (six receptions). -- Fowler

Who should they target? Broncos DL Sai'vion Jones. After trading away Simmons, the Titans should look for any young, highly drafted defensive linemen who haven't developed with their current teams. Jones might fit the bill, as he was unable to claim the defensive end spot across from Zach Allen this season. -- Schatz

Washington Commanders (2-4-1)
Chance to make playoffs: 11.6%

Projected first-round draft slot: No. 9

What is the deadline goal? Get better. It's an obvious goal for any team, but it's also how Washington views the situation and why the Commanders wouldn't consider themselves too active in looking to acquire or trade players based on their record. Even if, say, they lost to the Rams on Sunday and started to trade veterans on one-year deals for draft picks, they could still look to add talent, too -- not for this season alone but for the long hall. A player such as Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. would make sense. He has a high ceiling at a position they will need help at in 2027. Washington could also use more help at running back and offensive line. The Commanders have seven draft picks in 2027, the first time since 2024 that they have all of their selections. -- John Keim

Who could be on the move? Offensive tackle Andrew Wylie. Wylie is an swing-tackle type on an inexpensive contract who could be of interest in a market in which every team is looking for offensive line help and there's rarely any available. -- Graziano

Who should they target? Chargers RB Kimani Vidal. One spot at which Washington could use an upgrade is running back. Commanders running backs have amassed minus-69 rush yards over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Vidal has minus-2 RYOE this season as part of a three-man backfield in Los Angeles, but he flashed promise with 58 RYOE last season. -- Walder

stories.headline: Diogo Dalot: 'Everyone' at Man United should be feeling under pressure
stories.summary: Diogo Dalot has said that everyone at Manchester United should be feeling under pressure, not just head coach Michael Carrick, after a disappointing start to the season.
stories.body:
Diogo Dalot has said that everyone at Manchester United should be feeling under pressure, not just head coach Michael Carrick, after a disappointing start to the season.

United ended a run of nine games without a win on Tuesday after battling back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.

Carrick's job remains on the line ahead of Aston Villa's visit to Old Trafford on Sunday.

But Dalot insists it's not just the manager who should be feeling the heat with United 17th in the Premier League table and only above the relegation places on goal difference.

"Not just the manager, everyone is under pressure," said Dalot.

"I mean, when you don't win games for this football club, every moment, every person, everyone involved gets under pressure, and we felt it obviously, because we're not near good enough of what we should have done."

Victory over Roma brought to an end a run of three straight defeats, including miserable performances against Como and Bournemouth.

There was intense speculation around Carrick's position following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth with the 45-year-old ultimately given the chance to turn things around by the club's board.

"These moments are really tough, I'm not going to lie," said Dalot.

"Unfortunately, I've had a few moments like this in the past, and the only way for us to get out is by winning football games. I think that's the only way you can get confidence."

Carrick said the win over Roma was an "important night" but told his players they must build on the result against Villa this weekend.

It was only United's third victory of the season, but Dalot is hopeful that it can trigger a turnaround.

- Did Man United's Champions League comeback save Carrick's job?

- Michael Carrick: Man United comeback win over Roma 'an important night'

- Bruno Fernandes: Michael Carrick was right to drop me from Man United XI

"Nights like this can change momentum, can change seasons, and I think this win is going to give us confidence for the next games," he said.

"It's important from everyone around the club feeling that we care, that we want to turn this around, and I think we've shown, especially in the second 45 minutes, that we really want to turn this around."

stories.headline: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard completes knee treatment, begins 'return to play process'
stories.summary: Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced.
stories.body:
Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced Tuesday.

The team said it will provide an update on Leonard's progress in one week, meaning the earliest he could play again would be Nov. 11 against Boston.

Leonard, 35, was sidelined because of left knee swelling after appearing in just two regular-season games for Toronto. An MRI on the knee last month showed no structural damage.

Leonard has previously had issues with his right knee, having multiple surgeries for his meniscus and ACL.

In two games this season, Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals. He's in his first year back with the Raptors after being traded to Toronto from the LA Clippers this offseason after a scandal-marred conclusion to his six seasons there. He agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors after the trade.

Leonard previously played one season in Toronto, leading the Raptors to their only NBA championship in 2019 before leaving for the Clippers in free agency.

stories.headline: Outclassed by Barcelona, but Unai Emery's Aston Villa have plenty for Man United to envy
stories.summary: ESPN's Tom Hamilton explains why Aston Villa's defeat to Barcelona cannot overshadow Unai Emery's remarkable rebuild ahead of facing Man United.
stories.body:
BARCELONA, Spain -- It is credit to Unai Emery that as Aston Villa left the partially finished Camp Nou, they knew their performance in the 3-0 defeat to Barcelona wasn't a fair reflection of their project's progress. As you looked around ongoing redevelopment of the Camp Nou, and the 3,000 Villa fans getting soaked in the roofless stadium, you knew Villa's foundations are sturdy, the second tier robust and with a Europa League title as proof of progress. It's just that final level they're still trying to finesse. There's room for growth there, this team hasn't yet hit its ceiling.

The Villa fans were still drenched from the previous night's deluge as they traipsed through airport security in the early hours of Wednesday morning. They stood in Camp Nou near three hours, completely exposed to the elements as the rain hammered down and their hopes of a memorable result were slowly drowned by Barcelona's relentless press. It was a fantasy swallowed up by Raphinha, Lamine Yamal and their cohort of Blaugrana sharks, but also a missed opportunity due to their own self-inflicted mistakes. You can't give gifts away to a team who had already scored 57 goals in all competitions this season heading into last night's match, especially on Emery's 55th birthday.

"There are a lot of things to learn today," Emery said afterwards. "Overall we are competing fantastically in the Champions League; we have nine points. But today, we saw there is still more to do to get to this level."

But was the 3-0 defeat a reality check? Perhaps, but that is a bit too harsh. It's more likely this is just a nudge along the path in Villa's own evolution. "Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals," John McGinn said. "Tonight was a huge learning curve for us, and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future."

Emery spoke to the players post-match and hammered home the need to be clinical when it mattered -- whether that was passes around their own goal, or any sniff of an opportunity in the opposition's final third in an arena where seldom 50/50s go the way of the visiting team. He pointed to the errors, like the series which led to Barcelona's opener. It was six minutes in, Villa got flustered, constricted by Barcelona's high press. Zion Suzuki played a poorly-judged pass to João Gomes, who had Pedri breathing down his neck. Gomes' rushed pass went straight to Yamal, who set himself with a couple of lightning quick shimmies, flicked that wand of a left foot, curled the ball around Pau Torres and 1-0 Barça. Cue goal music and dancing in the rain. From there Villa were on the backfoot, in a match where they really had to knock Barça back with a few early punches rather than smack themselves in the face. Even more so given there were swathes of empty seats in the stands as several season ticket holders preferred to stay indoors rather than feel the brunt of the storm passing through Barcelona.

Villa had their chances at 1-0: Jackson had a one-on-one with Joan García which the keeper won. Gomes had a shot blocked by João Cancelo. Johan Manzambi scuffed an effort wide. Matty Cash came close with a volley. Manzambi fashioned another chance but shot straight at Garcia. Opportunities knocked but as Emery adds this Camp Nou tutorial to the litany of lessons he already has on several fruitless attempts at beating Barcelona on home turf (it's now one win out of 16 for Emery at Barcelona) it will be how his Villa team made the same mistakes again and again which would have annoyed him.

- Aston Villa left with 'lot of things to learn' after defeat in Barcelona

- Barcelona put on classy display to hand Aston Villa first UCL loss

- Prince William, Prince George watch on as Barcelona beat Aston Villa

They got caught out with slack passing from the back for Barcelona's opener and put together an ugly repeat of almost exactly the same move in the 26th minute where Suzuki's pass again found Gomes under pressure from Pedri, the ball coughed up, and this time it was Anthony Gordon who came close. And again, in the 66th minute, Suzuki's decision-making caused Villa bother, with Fermin pinching the ball off Boubacar Kamara and Suzuki produced a smart save to keep him out. As you look at Villa, that's one of the little ingredients missing: that ability to problem-solve mid-match in a tempest. "Today the test was not at the level we wanted to achieve, but left us a lot of things to learn, a lot of experiences for the players and it gives me information to analyse to try and compete at this level in hopefully the next months," Emery said.

"We have worked over four years together and we've made those mistakes before and we will always overcome those mistakes and improve as we know playing in this style is successful. We need to take those challenges and improve."

But let's take a step back. It's easy to pick holes in some of Villa's play last night, but what Emery has achieved in both the short and long-term since taking charge of the club in Oct. 2022 is a minor footballing miracle. He's helped build a sustainable, successful model at Villa, a team who have reached the Champions League in two of the last three seasons all under the constraints of the Premier League and UEFA's spending rules.

While he's steadily built Villa over the past four years, he's had to do some hasty repatching in the last four months. Since Villa had that historic night in Istanbul last May as they won the Europa League, the spine of that team has been picked apart. Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Emi Martinez, Lucas Digne and Youri Tielemans have all left.

The jigsaw Emery had to hastily re-assemble over the summer was formed off 11 new signings. Those pieces included an array of players at different stages in their career. Jackson and Aaron Wan-Bissaka arrived with points to prove, thrilling young talents like Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye brought promise but needed finessing, while he also recruited proven talents Suzuki and Matteo Ruggeri and Champions League-winning experience in Leon Goretzka. It's astute recruitment and a club confident in its process. "It was a very difficult start, a lot of change and information [the new signings have] taken in," McGinn said. "They realise the structure we've built in the four years the manager's been here gives players the best possible chance to show their ability and we've seen that with some of the new players, playing with much more confidence but most importantly playing for the team."

And if you want proof of the Emery effect and his incredible ability at maximising talent then take two case studies linked with Villa's next opponent Manchester United: Victor Lindelöf and Tielemans. When Villa picked up defender Lindelof on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, he'd just been released by United. By the following May, he was starring in Villa's midfield as they won the Europa League and has remained an important player back in his usual centre back role this term. And then on the flip side there's Tielemans who headed out of the Villa Park exit door in the summer.

"There are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them," Tielemans said at the time. He's since backtracked on those comments, and has looked fairly standard in a struggling United team. Emery elevates players like few other managers can. So you can imagine that when Villa travel to Old Trafford on Sunday, there'll be a few envious eyes cast from Manchester United's suits in the directors' box towards the man standing in Villa's dugout.

Emery has rebuilt Villa, again, in the space of four months. This is Emery 3.0: the first group evolved into 2.0, which won the Europa League, and now after the summer exodus, this is the next regeneration. Having that North Stand being rebuilt at Villa Park symbolizes where this club are -- one improving on sturdy ground, solid foundations, a club comfortable in being ambitious and expanding horizons.

"We have a demanding manager and coaching staff and they won't let us stop and be comfortable," McGinn said. "I'm 32 years old and the trajectory of this club is allowing me to dream in the same way I did since I was nine, 10, 11." Before Tuesday, McGinn's previous trip to the Camp Nou was in July 2004, as he took a stadium tour and coincidentally witnessed Ricardo Quaresma signing for Barça. Fast-forward 22 years, and on Tuesday night he led his team out onto the drenched, famous turf. That's progress.

Which is why as Villa's fans boarded their red-eye flights on Wednesday morning, having barely touched their hotel beds, they were quietly content. "It was one of those nights," said one fan, feet still squelching in sopping trainers. "We've come a long way," he added, gulping down a litre bottle of some fluorescent energy drink at 5.20am, his eyes telling the story of a night lived to the full. Even in defeat, these trips are to be savoured. They're still a novelty -- but they want these to become annual events.

On Sunday, Villa travel to Old Trafford. They'll still be licking their wounds at a missed opportunity, and lament self-inflicted errors. United will have the fillip of how they bounced back from 2-0 down to defeat Roma to give Michael Carrick another week in the job. As part of the match's narrative, there'll be inevitable talk of how Emery could be the answer to United's search for a saviour. But if you're Emery, would you rather fix holes in a ship that's been letting on water for 14 years, or stand atop the ocean liner you've helped craft with dry feet, surveying the various improvements being made and setting sail for whatever the horizon holds?

If you want to look at a club where steady progress is being made, a team comfortable in its own skin and completely aligned to one collective goal, then despite the colds and sniffles inevitably picked up as a byproduct of standing in a downpour for three hours on a chilly Tuesday evening, Villa are the team ahead of Sunday's trip to Old Trafford who are in rude health.

stories.headline: Skoda, main sponsor of ice hockey worlds, to 'reassess' backing if Russia plays
stories.summary: - The main sponsor of the men's ice hockey world championship, automaker Skoda, says it will "reassess" its backing for the tournament if Russia takes part.
stories.body:
DUESSELDORF, Germany -- The main sponsor of the men's ice hockey world championship, automaker Skoda, says it will "reassess" its backing for the tournament if Russia takes part.

The stance of Skoda, which has been the main sponsor for more than 30 years, puts more pressure on the International Ice Hockey Federation.

The IIHF said Wednesday that the impact of the ruling had been "significantly underestimated" and that it was still deciding how to react.

A Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling last week obliged the IIHF to lift its exclusion of Russian national teams, which had been in place since 2022 over the war in Ukraine.

Almost half of the 16 nations in the men's championship in Germany in May are refusing to play Russia. The Canadian government also says it will not allow Russia to compete at the world junior championship there starting next month.

"We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions," the Czechia-based automaker, which is part of Germany's Volkswagen Group, said in a statement Wednesday. "With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld.

"If the Russian national team takes part in the tournament, we will reassess our involvement in the tournament and take further action. We are actively monitoring the situation, remain in close contact with our partners and are confident that a constructive solution can be found."

Other sponsors have been critical of Russia's return. Nokian Tyres said it would end its backing if Russia takes part, and furniture maker AJ Products, a tournament sponsor since 1989, said Monday that it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

"The IIHF is aware of the recent statements made from key stakeholders regarding this decision and is carefully analyzing the scenarios around CAS's ruling," the federation said. "As presented to the CAS, the immediate reintegration of Russian teams presents significant practical and sporting challenges, including visa and entry requirements, security provisions, logistical constraints and consequences for competition formats, all compounded by the limited time available, with some events only weeks away.

"The global impact of the decision made by the CAS Panel and the challenges it creates for all involved were significantly underestimated."

Finland, Sweden, Czechia, Norway, Denmark and Latvia have said they will play the tournament but not games against Russia in a growing boycott since Finland declared its position Monday.

The Austrian federation became the seventh to join late Tuesday when its CEO Alexander Helwig told broadcaster ORF that "as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia" as part of broader European opposition.

Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev said in a statement via the Tass news agency Tuesday that he expected his country to be awarded wins if other nations forfeit games and that Russia would send information to the International Olympic Committee about potential boycotts and the conduct of host nations.

stories.headline: MLB proposes delaying salary cap until 2028 season
stories.summary: Major League Baseball has proposed delaying the implementation of a salary cap until 2028 while it puts into place other elements of its labor offer for 2027.
stories.body:
Major League Baseball on Tuesday proposed postponing the implementation of a salary cap until the 2028 season while still putting into place the other elements of its labor offer for 2027 as the current collective bargaining agreement approaches its Dec. 1 expiration.

With the MLB Players Association consistently voicing its objection to any cap, the league has pressed forward with its pursuit of a cap and floor. But the opening of free agency Monday, and the significant likelihood of MLB locking out the players when the current labor deal expires, complicated the ability of teams to plan amid the uncertain labor landscape and prompted the proposed delay, sources told ESPN.

The $258.2 million cap and $180.2 million floor that the league projected for 2028 in a meeting with the union Tuesday was higher than the $245.3 million and $171.2 million numbers proposed by MLB as its original cap-and-floor offer for 2027. The new numbers reflect a 50-50 split on projected 2028 revenue, with the calculation of player share including hundreds of millions of dollars in amateur signing bonuses as well as deductions by teams that other major men's leagues use in their cap-and-floor systems.

MLB also proposed giving $282 million in competitive balance tax proceeds to players in cash payments, sources said. Players are entitled to 50% of proceeds, according to the current collective bargaining agreement, that are used to fully fund players' 401(k) accounts. IRS limits cap the present-day distribution at around $72 million, according to sources. Because of increased spending beyond the $244 million competitive balance tax threshold, hundreds of millions of dollars in excess owed to players sit in reserve.

Union officials have said players would lose more than $1 billion over the life of the league's proposal if they agreed to a cap, reflecting the chasm between the parties that could lead to a prolonged work stoppage.

MLB locked out players in December 2021, leading to a 99-day stoppage that ended in mid-March 2022. In late May of this year, the league formally proposed a cap-and-floor system for the first time since 1994, when players went on strike for 232 days, the World Series was canceled and baseball returned to the field after players avoided an overhaul to the game's economic system through legal challenges.

Under the league's proposal Tuesday, competitive balance tax thresholds -- a luxury tax mechanism used to penalize teams with higher payrolls -- would remain the same for the 2027 season. While the 2028 cap-and-floor numbers are projections, 12 teams -- including the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers -- would need to increase their payrolls to reach the floor. Eight teams carried payrolls that would have been in excess of the ceiling.

Teams would not be forced to reach the floor in any given year under the league's proposal. They would be permitted to spend as little as 90% of the floor number, as long as over multiple years their spending reflects a minimum agreed-upon number.

The MLBPA has proposed maintaining the current framework of the league's financial system while significantly increasing spending, reflected by a base competitive balance tax threshold of $300 million, a $56 million rise from the current number. Additionally, the union has asked for a surge in the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1.5 million, a $180 million pre-arbitration bonus pool -- it's currently at $50 million -- and free agency for players 30 and older after five years of major league service, not six.

The league, contingent on the acceptance of a cap-and-floor system, has said it would agree to earlier free agency for those 30 and older, while proposing a $900,000 minimum (with some players receiving $1 million) and a $65 million pre-arbitration bonus pool. MLB also has proposed significant changes to amateur entry, implementing an international draft, removing high school players from the domestic draft and slashing domestic draft bonuses, all of which the union opposes.

"Coming off another incredible season of baseball, MLB owners continue to propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values," the MLBPA said in a statement. "... Players stand ready to negotiate in good faith toward a new CBA that will capitalize on our sport's unprecedented momentum and benefit players, clubs, and fans alike."

MLB, in a statement explaining its proposal to delay a cap by a year, said it recognized that teams need a full offseason to prepare to operate within the cap-and-floor system.

"This proposal would allow a smoother transition into the cap and floor system without delaying key player benefits, including earlier free agency, a $1 million minimum salary, a 30% increase to the pre-arbitration bonus pool, and transactional reform that will reduce roster churn," the statement said. "The projected salary cap and floor for 2028 continues to provide more money for major league players while leveling the playing field and giving more teams the ability to participate in the free agent market and retain their homegrown stars so that every fan believes their team has a fair chance to win it all."

stories.headline: Liberty coach Chris DeMarco is out: Next candidates for New York
stories.summary: The Liberty are searching for a coach for a second straight offseason. What went wrong, and what's next?
stories.byline: Alexa Philippou and Michael Voepel and Kendra Andrews
stories.body:
Three days after crowning its 2026 champion, the WNBA was back in the news. Chris DeMarco will not be retained as head coach of the New York Liberty, sources told ESPN on Tuesday.

The Liberty will have a third head coach in as many years; the franchise previously moved on from Sandy Brondello in September 2025, one season removed from New York winning its first WNBA title.

"We need to nail this," Liberty general manager Jonathan Kolb said at the time, two months before hiring DeMarco. "If we're going to make a bold decision like this, our players deserve to get the best, and so we'll take the time necessary."

DeMarco came to Brooklyn after spending over a decade on staff with the Golden State Warriors and serving as head coach of the Bahamas men's basketball team since 2019.

His one season in New York was rather rocky. The Liberty won the Commissioner's Cup in late June but were 13-12 just before the All-Star break. They finished the season 26-18 -- their worst win percentage in a season since signing Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones in 2023 -- and earned the eighth and final seed in the playoffs, where they swept the No. 1 Minnesota Lynx but then were swept in turn by the No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream in the semifinals.

This is the third consecutive offseason that a WNBA coach has been let go after one year; it happened with Teresa Weatherspoon in Chicago (2024) and Chris Koclanes in Dallas (2025). But DeMarco is the first noninterim coach to win a playoff series in his first season and not return to coach the same team.

But New York has sky-high internal and external expectations. After the Liberty were eliminated in the semis -- a second straight year without a Finals appearance -- the Liberty's stars reiterated their desire to not just compete for championships but win them. So what's next for New York as the franchise looks for a new coach for the second offseason in a row? ESPN analyzes how the Liberty got here and how they move forward.

What went wrong for DeMarco in his first season?
Philippou: On paper, firing a coach who went 26-18 and swept the No. 1 seed in the first round of the playoffs might seem surprising, but it felt like this was the outcome New York was headed toward especially given how its season ended -- and with none of the Liberty's stars going to bat for their coach.

It seemed like there was a legitimate learning curve with DeMarco and his staff's first season in the WNBA. He spoke in his introductory news conference about ordering every book on the Liberty and having to learn about the history of the WNBA. And while he had experience as head coach of the Bahamas national team, coaching in sporadic FIBA windows is not the same as the grind of a 44-game regular season.

It was notable that Stewart critiqued the team for being too inconsistent this year. "This is not like cramming for a test. You got to be ready and ready to go since the jump," she said in response to a question about DeMarco's future.

There were some positives, like how DeMarco reset the Liberty's offense -- they were one of the better offensive teams in the league in the second half of the season. But even once Leonie Fiebich returned from injury, they were far from an elite defensive team, needed to be a true contender.

It often felt like Stewart took on more of a burden in leading the team than DeMarco. That was especially evident in how she was the one who spoke out the most after Game 2 of the semifinals, when the Liberty thought officials said they did not have a reset timeout to use at the end of overtime when they actually had one. Even in the aftermath, Sabrina Ionescu took more public accountability than DeMarco for not stopping the game to get clarity on whether New York had the timeout.

New York would not make the decision to part ways with DeMarco if it had felt Year 2 would be better than Year 1 under a new head coach. We'll see what the organization has in mind for its next hire, but it seems it did not have enough faith he could grow into the leader it needed by next season.

Andrews: There were a lot of moments leading up to Tuesday's move, but the lasting image of DeMarco's stint in New York is the blundered reset timeout Alexa mentions above. That mishandling of the closing seconds led to a crucial loss, but perhaps even more striking was the response afterwards. Instead of DeMarco taking ownership of his mistake, the players spoke up. It was a strange peek inside the leadership of the Liberty, and it felt like a nail in the coffin.

There were questions about how much knowledge DeMarco had about the WNBA since he was introduced as the head coach last winter. And that moment in the playoffs felt like a prime example of his lack of experience in the WNBA.

Voepel: Maybe DeMarco didn't realize how fast Kolb would pull the plug on him, so he thought he would have more time to adjust to the WNBA. But we can look at something Kolb said last year when the Liberty parted with Brondello.

"This is not a results-based organization," Kolb said in late September 2025 in explaining the decision. "This is not about not winning or winning. It's about how do we position ourselves to be at the top of the league in a real sustainable way as the league evolves."

In short, it seemed like Kolb didn't believe Brondello was innovative enough for a changing league. He apparently believed DeMarco was, but that didn't turn out to Kolb's and the Liberty's satisfaction, either.

So, whoever takes this job next has to understand what Kolb wants in terms of everyday results (which do matter) and also what meets the GM's definition of "sustainable" innovation. DeMarco probably thought he would get more of a chance to prove himself in both respects.

Who are the early candidates to be New York's next coach?

Voepel: In 2024, Brondello led the Liberty to the first WNBA championship in the organization's then 28-year history. After a first-round playoff exit in 2025, she was let go, despite seeming to have the support of Stewart. Now DeMarco is out. How does all that impact how appealing this job is?

One avenue for New York is a former NBA assistant. Becky Hammon (Las Vegas) and Natalie Nakase (Golden State) both came from those ranks, and both have won championships as WNBA head coaches. Hammon even played 16 seasons in the WNBA.

Accordingly, one name could be Los Angeles Lakers assistant coach Lindsey Harding, the former Duke star who was the WNBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2007. She played nine seasons in the WNBA, then began her coaching career as a scout and development coach with the Philadelphia 76ers. She also had a stint with the Sacramento Kings before joining the Lakers. It would seem likely that the Liberty will at least gauge her interest.

Another path could be what the Atlanta Dream did with Karl Smesko: Going to the college ranks to find a coach who knows the women's game well and is ready to move to the pro ranks. But, again, job security (or lack thereof) could be an obstacle.

Philippou: To Voepel's point, hiring someone who lacked familiarity with the WNBA and women's basketball came back to bite New York, so Kolb could target someone who checks those boxes. He could look at a NBA or WNBA assistant ready for a head coach role, but that begs the question of whether an inexperienced head coach is the right fit for this title-minded group and a limited championship window.

New York likes to go big, so it wouldn't be shocking for them to check in with the likes of Hammon and Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White. (Nakase would have been on that list too had the Valkyries not literally just won a championship.)

In addition to finding a new coach, what are the other offseason priorities for the franchise?

Philippou: It is quite possible the Liberty's roster will look fairly different in 2027. Stewart, Jones, Ionescu, Fiebich and Satou Sabally all remain under contract, as does French rookie Marine Fauthoux, who had a breakout semifinal series against the Dream.

New York will want an update on the status of Sabally, who had to step away from the court this summer to deal with the effects of her second concussion in a year. There has been no word publicly on when she might return to the court.

Ionescu also had a tough year health-wise, so this season will be all about her getting healthy. Her struggles in 2026 put much more of a burden on Stewart, especially, to be great every single night; but, longer term, Stewart will need more help if this team wants to win another championship.

That said, most of the Liberty's supporting cast will be free agents this offseason, including Pauline Astier, Marine Johannes and Han Xu. It wouldn't be shocking to see Kolb overhaul the bench and look to bolster the team's wing depth.

In the wake of the Liberty's semifinal elimination, New York players spoke more generally about what they want to see in future roster construction.

"It just took a while to find our identity, what we were going to do defensively and how we were going to play with teams," Stewart said. "When people say defense wins championships, it's f---ing true."

Added Fiebich, who lamented the loss of Nyara Sabally and Kayla Thornton in the last two expansion drafts: "We won in 2024 because we brought the toughness and we had the talent and we had the team chemistry. I think we've got to continue to find ways to get that back."

stories.headline: Robert Lewandowski's jersey outselling Lionel Messi's since Chicago arrival
stories.summary: Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in MLS since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Miami kit.
stories.body:
Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in Major League Soccer since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Inter Miami kit.

MLS' 10 best-selling jerseys of 2026 was revealed by the league on Tuesday, with Messi still No. 1 overall but with former Barcelona and Bayern Munich star Lewandowski making a big impact.

- MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up

- Messi brings Miami back to stun Revs, clinch Champions Cup spot

- Nashville ties Miami's single-season points record with 1 game to go

Lewandowski officially signed with Chicago on June 29, and made his MLS debut on July 22 against Inter Miami.

The Poland international has recorded seven goals and added five assists in 18 games, propelling the Fire to fourth place on the Eastern Conference table and a place in the playoffs.

Miami captain Messi, however, leads sales through all of 2026, earning first place for the fourth consecutive season. Messi first topped the list in 2023, just months after signing with Inter Miami in July of that year.

stories.headline: Luana Santos comes to grips with rise in women's bantamweight rankings

After all nine of her takedown attempts were fended off in the first round, Santos went right back to leaning on her judo background in the two rounds that followed, landing five takedowns and amassing 7½ minutes of control time and winning her fourth fight in a row.
