stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: Watching successor Kimi Antonelli win title 'highlight of my year'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.

Antonelli, who replaced the seven-time world champion at Mercedes at the start of 2025 following his move to Ferrari, clinched the title at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest champion in F1 history at just 20 years old.

Hamilton, along with fellow multiple title-winner Max Verstappen, celebrated Antonelli's achievement on the podium and praised the Italian in a post on social media on Monday.

"Let me start with a huge congratulations to the new champion, Kimi Antonelli," Hamilton, 41, wrote on Instagram. "To have seen your journey so closely and to be there celebrating with you, was a highlight of my year. So well deserved and a record that will stand for a long time.

"It was great to see your team at Mercedes celebrating with you. Enjoy this moment, keep your family close, keep your passion and your energy."

Antonelli was just 18 when he stepped into Hamilton's seat at Mercedes, facing the daunting task of replacing the most successful driver in F1 history, who won six of his seven world titles with the Silver Arrows.

But the Italian has enjoyed a remarkable second season, beating teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Hamilton -- among others -- to the championship with four rounds still scheduled to take place.

Hamilton's congratulations came alongside an admission of frustration over Ferrari's weekend in Mexico, where he felt the team had missed an opportunity to win and also appeared to acknowledge tensions following Charles Leclerc's actions on the opening laps.

"Our own weekend was one full of challenges," Hamilton said. "We had a lot thrown at us but our mechanics and engineers did an incredible job.

"We've grown so much together this year, and that progress has taken a huge effort from everyone on the track and back at the factory. That's why losing what could've been a win hurts so much.

"We need to grasp every opportunity we have, so it's incredibly frustrating, and I can't pretend otherwise."

- Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari have 'big problems' after Charles Leclerc incident

- Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari, questions Leclerc's 'mentality'

He added: "Battling is necessary, but when that battle costs the team, we have to be honest about it and learn from it.

"We can push each other to the limit and still honour the responsibility to everyone who put us on that track."

Despite his frustrations, Hamilton insisted his commitment to Ferrari remained unchanged.

"I'll keep giving everything I have. My belief in this team hasn't changed and neither has my responsibility to help us get this right," he said.

"Stick with us. I'm only just getting started with this team, and we have so much more to come."

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: North Sydney Bears royalty lands in Perth to lead new NRL club
stories.summary: Tony Rea is a man who doesn't mince his words and has been entrusted as the Perth Bears' new chief executive as the club prepares to make its NRL debut.
stories.body:
The Jillaroos are their own biggest critics after a performance that produced the biggest margin of victory in international women's rugby league history. The Australian side steamrolled through Wales in a 124-6 win on Sunday that saw winger Jaime Chapman match another record, her six-try haul equalling the mark for most tries in a game for the Jillaroos.

The toppling of Wales came on the back of a 78-0 thrashing of England and 40-0 thumping of Samoa.

But the Jillaroos are intent on dissecting what they need to improve.

The performance could absolutely have been better, winger Abbi Church insisted at training on Wednesday.

"No performance is perfect, and there's always things that we can improve on," Church said.

"What we're trying to be in this camp is to be the best.

"(We) reflect on our own performances and be quite critical and look to where we can improve individually and as a team."

Sunday's win secured Australia's in the semi-finals on Sunday against Fiji and the side aren't buying into the bookmakers belief that it'll be another walk in the park.

In their World Cup pool, Fiji pummelled Papua New Guinea 40-4 and France 54-6, after giving New Zealand a run for their money and falling short in an 18-12 loss.

Church said the Jillaroos squad watched that game with a close eye.

"We know that Fiji did put in quite a fight against New Zealand," she told the media.

"We know they're going to come out this week and we have to obviously be prepared for that".

Coach Jess Skinner believes it will be challenging to face off against a Fiji side carrying so much belief and an underdog mentality.

Fiji are a dangerous side that are quick with the ball, Skinner said after the Wales win..

"They've had an outstanding campaign, and what they did to the Kiwis put the rest of the competition on notice.

"We'll go to another level this week, do our due diligence to make sure that we're prepared best on both sides of the ball for them.''

stories.headline: John Harbaugh pushing all the right buttons for Giants
stories.summary: The coach's culture of accountability and expectations has New York (4-2-1) in first place in the NFC East.
stories.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Giants entered their Week 8 bye week having matched their win total from last year -- before the midway point of the season.

Something has changed, beginning with the coach. John Harbaugh and his staff have pushed all the right buttons early this season while developing a culture and setting expectations. It has the Giants (4-2-1) in first place in the NFC East.

Accountability is vital in Harbaugh's program. This is crucial because it was considered a shortcoming of former coach Brian Daboll and how he led the team. These new Giants are at a point where it's acceptable and common during team meetings for Harbaugh or his assistants to call out individuals for mistakes during practice or games.

Uncomfortable, sure, but they don't let it fester. Instead, they make it imperative it gets fixed. Communication is key.

This was evident just last week when defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson was unhappy with his unit's effort in running to chase down plays in a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. The film showed players slacking and not putting in maximum effort to the whistle. Rather than addressing it individually or during the defensive meeting, it was addressed in front of the entire room.

"You confront it. Just like we do, we confront everything," Wilson said. "When you're in the meeting room, you show those plays. I look at guys that don't run to the ball, and I call them traitors because they're traitors to the defense. At the end of the day, when you have a traitor to the defense, you either have to make adjustments to get them off the field, you have to get somebody else on the field, or they have to correct their behaviors."

Harbaugh and his coaching staff haven't been shy about making lineup changes, if necessary. Already this season quarterback Jameis Winston, running back Cam Skattebo, center John Michael Schmitz Jr., defensive linemen Darius Alexander and CJ Okoye, cornerback Paulson Adebo and safety Tyler Nubin have been removed from the lineup at times. Harbaugh doesn't like the word "benched," but in most cases that is effectively what it has been. Salary or veteran standing doesn't stand in the way either. Not in Harbaugh's program.

The only thing that seems to matter is what gives Harbaugh's team the best chance to win. That's how he explained the switch from Winston to J.J. McCarthy last week at quarterback. The move gave the Giants the best chance to beat the Houston Texans that week.

As a matter of fact, Harbaugh was so nonchalant about the move that he didn't make any grand announcement to his team. Many of the players found out about the quarterback change when they started going over the game plan.

Mistakes on the field are a different animal. They are unacceptable and handled bluntly at team meetings.

"We have a bunch of good guys," Harbaugh said. "Our guys understand that we have to confront everything that has to do with our football, and if we do that, that comes from a place of love because we care enough, we all care enough, and we need to hear it too, as coaches, and we did from our players. There are plenty of things that our players talk to us about that they want to see done better from a coaching perspective, and if we have that kind of relationship, that kind of partnership, coaches and players, to me, you just have a chance to be successful because you build trust that way.

"I just am appreciative of the fact that everybody in the building made it about what's important, which is the football. That's what we have to continue to do, and we will continue to do that. We've all seen it be successful."

Not every coach handles it the same way but it's easier to accept given Harbaugh's results in Baltimore and now early in New York. Daboll once held a team meeting after a blowout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers where he only showed the positive plays.

Different strokes for different folks.

"I would say some of [my coaches] have handled it like Harbaugh, some of them haven't. It really just depends on your coaching style and how you want to handle it," veteran offensive lineman Aaron Stinnie said. "But I think guys are taking really good to it and like it. I think it helps. It helps keep everyone accountable and stay on the same page.

"There's definitely a way to do it and he does a good job of having it in a constructive manner. Just being upfront and honest. Everything is transparency."

This is what the Giants were buying when hiring Harbaugh. They got a coach with a track record of success who knows what it takes to win football games. It's no accident they are 3-1-1 in games decided by one score or less one year after finishing 1-7 in those such games last season.

Harbaugh has found ways to get the most out of his players, whether it be calling out guys for lack of effort at team meetings or demoting someone like Skattebo for fumbling. Skattebo rebounded by setting a career high with 124 rushing yards in a 27-21 win against the Houston Texans on Sunday.

"I don't know if it's philosophy so much," Harbaugh said of his tactics. "It's just a week-to-week feel thing with your guys."

Harbaugh can downplay it all he wants. This is what players such as tight end Isaiah Likely, who came over with him from Baltimore, said back in the spring that he does best. The new Giants coach is a wizard with his messaging and so far he's getting the most out of his players, teams and coaches.

It has resulted in the Giants winning despite losing their quarterback, Jaxson Dart, and best defensive player, Brian Burns, due to injury. It has cornerback Deonte Banks playing the best football of his career after two disastrous seasons. It has offensive coordinator Matt Nagy scheming players open with regularity despite being on his third starting quarterback in seven games and Wilson transforming in and out of being a blitz-happy team depending on the week and opponent.

Key to this success is the way they are handling business.

"If you're not doing something to help the team and you're hurting the team, if your effort is bad, if you have a lack of toughness, it gets pointed out. And it gets pointed out in front of everybody, not only in a defensive meeting. It gets pointed out in the full team meeting," Wilson said. "When you have behaviors that's unacceptable, we're not going to accept it. And if you don't change the behaviors, we have to change the players."

The message is being received.

stories.headline: Carlos Baleba injury 'doesn't look great' - Man United boss Michael Carrick
stories.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said Carlos Baleba's injury "doesn't look great" after the midfielder was forced off during Tuesday's 3-2 win over Roma.
stories.body:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said Carlos Baleba's injury "doesn't look great" after the midfielder was forced off during Tuesday's 3-2 win over Roma.

Baleba appeared to be in tears after pulling up holding his hamstring only moments into the second half at Old Trafford.

The 22-year-old was consoled by Carrick as he left the pitch and United's head coach hinted that he's expecting a long lay-off for the £70 million ($94m) summer signing.

"I haven't got any more news on Carlos at this stage," said Carrick.

"It's his hamstring, so we'll just have to assess what that looks like. Initially, it doesn't look great. Timelines, I haven't got much more to give you."

Baleba was making just his fifth United start after his debut was delayed by an ankle picked up during his preseason with Brighton.

stories.headline: NBA Power Rankings: Summing up all 30 teams' starts
stories.summary: Here's where all 30 NBA teams rank after two weeks of action, plus the four words used to describe how each team has started the season.
stories.body:
Just two weeks into the NBA season, storylines have been flipped as injuries and surprise surges reverberate around the league.

The Philadelphia 76ers have dominated their opponents early -- and are having some fun in the process. Meanwhile, the reigning champion New York Knicks are attempting to claw themselves back into the top echelon after starting the season 0-3.

It's in the West where things have started to heat up. The Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves are dealing with injuries to their stars, making way for players such as the Memphis Grizzlies' Ty Jerome to have an early impact in his team's standings. The Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic is making an early MVP case and doesn't seem to be slowing down after scoring 42 and 45 points in his past two games. And the Portland Trail Blazers, sans Ja Morant as he deals with an injury, are showing that depth is what will set teams apart across the league.

In our second iteration of Power Rankings since the season started, our NBA insiders assigned four words to describe each team's start to 2026-27, and break down why things are -- or are not -- working.

Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Ben Golliver, Kris Rhim and Anthony Slater) think teams belong.

1. Houston Rockets

2026-27 record: 7-1
Previous ranking: 4
Next games: vs. MIN (Nov. 4), @ PHX (Nov. 7), vs. DEN (Nov. 9)

VanVleet's impact is immeasurable. The Rockets navigated the choppy waters of Kevin Durant's first season nearly rudderless without floor general Fred VanVleet, who sustained a season-ending knee injury before the start of training camp. Now that he's back, Houston is a calmer, more organized team. VanVleet directs traffic, manipulates defenses to set up teammates for shots in their preferred spots and limits turnovers, catalyzing a Houston offense with the league's best rating (121.2).

Wisely, the Rockets added ballhandling insurance with another veteran point guard in Marcus Smart, who can start in VanVleet's place when he sits the second night of back-to-backs. -- Michael C. Wright

2. Detroit Pistons

2026-27 record: 6-1
Previous ranking: 3
Next games: vs. PHI (Nov. 4), vs. LAL (Nov. 8), vs. WAS (Nov. 9)

3-pointers have improved. The Pistons have developed a reputation for stifling defense and it hasn't changed, being first in points per game against and defensive rating. What has seemed to improve early is their 3-point shooting.

Cade Cunningham is carrying over his playoff 3-point shooting with a career-high 37%, and Kevin Huerter, who struggled after coming from Chicago at midseason, is at a more-than-respectable clip of 38.5% (he shot 29% in 25 games last season). Duncan Robinson is No. 4 in makes, and the team collectively has risen to No. 6 in percentage (38.1). Their season high in triples in a game in 2025-26 was 18, a mark they've matched twice in the first two weeks. -- Vince Goodwill

3. Philadelphia 76ers

2026-27 record: 7-1
Previous ranking: 5
Next games: @ DET (Nov. 4), @ CLE (Nov. 6), @ CHI (Nov. 8), vs. BOS (Nov. 10)

The Tyrese Maxey Show. Maxey has been Philly's best player while being on a team with two former MVPs, LeBron James and Joel Embiid, and a Finals MVP in Jaylen Brown. The 25-year-old leads the Sixers in scoring and has buoyed them late in games this season with explosive fourth quarters that have kept them winning. He leads the NBA in fourth-quarter scoring (11.0).

"I just think he now feels -- like in a nonarrogant and even a humble way -- he knows he's really, really good," coach Nick Nurse said of Maxey. "And I'm not sure that was always the case." -- Kris Rhim

4. Boston Celtics

2026-27 record: 5-2
Previous ranking: 8
Next games: vs. MIL (Nov. 4), @ CHA (Nov. 6), @ MIL (Nov. 8), @ PHI (Nov. 10)

They'll be just fine. The Celtics traded All-NBA forward Brown fresh off his best season for 36-year-old Paul George this offseason, a return that came as somewhat of a surprise considering George appears to be declining.

But through the first two weeks, George has fit in with the Celtics seamlessly as the team has looked like a contender in the Eastern Conference. George is averaging 20.7 points, six rebounds and five assists. Coach Joe Mazzulla recently praised George's impact for being "beyond what's happening on the offensive end," pointing to George's leadership. -- Rhim

5. San Antonio Spurs

2026-27 record: 5-2
Previous ranking: 9
Next games: vs. DAL (Nov. 4), @ SAC (Nov. 6), @ POR (Nov. 7), @ PHX (Nov. 9)

Still working through kinks. San Antonio expected that, coming into the season, it would have to work through some hiccups with its new starting lineup, but Spurs coach Mitch Johnson is committed to seeing it through. And slowly, the group is starting to deliver on the promise Johnson saw when pondering whether to put them all together.

Of course, Victor Wembanyama is at the center of it all, and San Antonio's dynamic guards are finding more ways to get him shots closer to the basket. Wembanyama currently leads the NBA in made alley-oops, averaging 3.8 per game, more than twice the average of any other player. -- Wright

6. Memphis Grizzlies

2026-27 record: 6-1
Previous ranking: 14
Next games: vs. IND (Nov. 4), vs. OKC (Nov. 6), @ TOR (Nov. 9)

Kleiman "conviction" is confirmed. After last season's trade deadline, Grizzlies general manager Zach Kleiman expressed confidence in what was left in Memphis after jettisoning key players -- Desmond Bane the previous summer and later Jaren Jackson Jr. -- from a roster previously expected to contend for years to come.

Kleiman moved the final player, Ja Morant, in June. But on that February day, Kleiman discussed his "conviction" in "pivoting to a younger build" that was "not going to be some drawn-out five-year process." Perhaps he was right, considering Memphis' 6-1 start behind young players such as Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward taking on major roles alongside a resurgent Ty Jerome.-- Wright

7. Los Angeles Lakers

2026-27 record: 6-2
Previous ranking: 6
Next games: @ SAC (Nov. 4), vs. POR (Nov. 6), @ DET (Nov. 8), @ ATL (Nov. 9)

Luka's on a heater It's hard to imagine a better start to the season for the Slovenian sharpshooter, leading the league in scoring with 38.3 points per game on percentage splits of 49.7/42.7/88.7. After he scored 42 in a rout of the Heat on Monday, Giannis Antetokounmpo wondered aloud whether Doncic wasn't just establishing himself as the best scorer in today's game, but rather the best to ever put the ball in the basket in the history of the game.

Most encouraging for L.A., the points have come with wins. The Lakers are 6-2 out of the gates. -- Dave McMenamin

8. Portland Trail Blazers

2026-27 record: 5-1
Previous ranking: 10
Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 4), @ LAL (Nov. 6), vs. SA (Nov. 7), vs. OKC (Nov. 10)

Rolling along without Ja. While critics of Portland's offseason trade for Morant questioned his fit in a crowded backcourt, it pays to have extra depth in the modern NBA. Countless teams are struggling to cope with early-season injuries to key players, but the Blazers have maintained their positive momentum despite losing Morant to a strained hamstring after only four games. Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard kept the offense humming throughout a convincing road win over Denver on Monday.

Meanwhile, Scoot Henderson has stepped into Morant's starting spot to bolster Portland's perimeter defense, and veteran Jrue Holiday has thrived as a selfless sixth man. -- Ben Golliver

9. Cleveland Cavaliers

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 13
Next games: @ OKC (Nov. 4), vs. PHI (Nov. 6), vs. NYK (Nov. 7), @ CHA (Nov. 9)

Still figuring themselves out. The good news is Cleveland has more wins than losses; the bad news is the Cavaliers haven't looked that smooth in the process, with Peyton Watson in particular struggling to jell with his new squad. Cleveland has plenty of time to find its form, but the early returns are mixed rather than overwhelmingly positive. -- Zach Kram

10. Oklahoma City Thunder

2026-27 record: 5-2
Previous ranking: 1
Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 4), @ MEM (Nov. 6), vs. WAS (Nov. 7), @ POR (Nov. 10)

Injuries are adding up. The injuries to four All-Defensive players -- Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren and Alex Caruso -- have robbed the Thunder of one of their offensive superpowers. The Thunder have averaged only 11.8 points off of turnovers in the past four games, which ranks third to last in the league during that span.

By contrast, Oklahoma City led the NBA in points off of turnovers in each of the past three seasons. -- Tim MacMahon

11. Minnesota Timberwolves

2026-27 record: 5-3
Previous ranking: 2
Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 4), @ NO (Nov. 6), vs. UTAH (Nov. 8)

Come back soon, Ant. The Timberwolves are hanging tough without Anthony Edwards, who is expected to sit out two months after undergoing a knee procedure. Without their franchise guard, the Timberwolves struggled to sustain their newfound happy-go-lucky vibes during losses to the Warriors and Spurs. But Minnesota did take care of business against the Clippers and Bucks -- two projected bottom-dwellers -- to keep its head above water.

Ayo Dosunmu, who signed a five-year, $112 million contract this summer, will get the chance to prove his worth while starting in place of Edwards. -- Golliver

12. Golden State Warriors

2026-27 record: 5-3
Previous ranking: 27
Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 5), vs. ORL (Nov. 7), vs. NO (Nov. 9)

Yaxel Lendeborg has arrived. The No. 11 pick in June's draft has already scored 26, 26, 31 and 37 points in his first two weeks in the NBA. His latest outburst, which included six 3s, came in a win over the LA Clippers in which Stephen Curry and Draymond Green rested. This Warriors team just followed an 0-3 start with a sudden five-game surge, and Curry, after the fifth straight win, was asked what changed.

"Yax," Curry said. The Warriors didn't win five straight all of last season. The Warriors drafted a 24-year-old, 6-foot-10 power wing who has immediately looked like a top-30ish player in the NBA.

"Changes everything," coach Steve Kerr said. -- Anthony Slater

13. Dallas Mavericks

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 22
Next games: @ SA (Nov. 4), vs. UTAH (Nov. 6), vs. BKN (Nov. 8), vs. IND (Nov. 9)

Flagg is taking off. Cooper Flagg's ascent to becoming an elite scorer hit a speed bump in Monday's loss to the previously winless Kings, when the 19-year-old went 3-of-19 from the field. Flagg is still averaging 25.2 points this season.

The only players in NBA history to average that many points at age 20 or younger: LeBron James, Luka Doncic, Kevin Durant and Zion Williamson. -- MacMahon

14. Toronto Raptors

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 7
Next games: @ DEN (Nov. 4), @ MIL (Nov. 6), vs. MEM (Nov. 9)

Life without Kawhi, again. After reacquiring Leonard in a trade this offseason, the Raptors have already been forced to deal with the reality of Leonard: one of the league's best players who has been consistently sidelined because of left knee swelling.

Still, the Raptors have remained afloat thanks to Scottie Barnes, who is ninth in steals per game (2.1) and 13th in scoring (24.4), and a historically suffocating defense that leads the league with 20.9 turnovers per game. -- Rhim

15. Denver Nuggets

2026-27 record: 3-3
Previous ranking: 12
Next games: vs. TOR (Nov. 4), @ IND (Nov. 7), @ HOU (Nov. 9)

A lone bright spot. Among several problems that emerged for the Nuggets in last April's first-round flameout to the injured Minnesota Timberwolves, Jamal Murray's lack of production was perhaps the most destructive. He shot 35.7% in the series, 26.2% on 3s and petered out in a 12-point elimination Game 6, missing 13 of 17 shots. That memory appears flushed to open the season. Murray is one of the hottest scorers in the NBA, averaging 27.3 points and making more than 50% of his 3s.

Even so, the Nuggets are a wobbly 3-3, with a remarkably average offense, considering they still have Nikola Jokic manning the middle. They led the NBA with a 121.2 offensive rating last season. They're currently 16th at 112.6. -- Slater

16. Washington Wizards

2026-27 record: 4-3
Previous ranking: 18
Next games: vs. ATL (Nov. 4), @ ATL (Nov. 6), @ OKC (Nov. 7), @ DET (Nov. 9)

That's everything Washington could have wanted from the two No. 1 picks so far. -- Kram

2026-27 record: 3-4
Previous ranking: 16
Next games: vs. CHI (Nov. 4), @ CLE (Nov. 7), vs. MIL (Nov. 10)

The Mikal Bridges question. The curious case of Bridges continues to start the season, culminating in him playing only 16 minutes against the Nets on Monday night. It's a small sample size, but he's averaging career lows in scoring and efficiency, and even his 3-point attempts are down. The Knicks made a concerted effort to get him going, but it seemed futile.

"He's just got to keep playing," Knicks coach Mike Brown said. "Everybody goes through those ups and downs throughout the course of the season, and obviously, it's the beginning of the season right now, so he's got to find his way.

2026-27 record: 4-4
Previous ranking: 15
Next games: @ WAS (Nov. 4), vs. WAS (Nov. 6), vs. BKN (Nov. 7), vs. LAL (Nov. 9)

What won't appear is Cleveland playing in the second night of a back-to-back and Indiana having only six healthy players. The Pacers became the first team to have six players available this early in the season since the 1948 Boston Celtics. -- Bobby Marks

2026-27 record: 2-5
Previous ranking: 24
Next games: @ LAC (Nov. 4), @ GS (Nov. 5), @ SAC (Nov. 8), @ UTAH (Nov. 10)

20. Charlotte Hornets

2026-27 record: 3-5
Previous ranking: 17
Next games: @ BKN (Nov. 4), vs. BOS (Nov. 6), vs. CLE (Nov. 9)

21. Orlando Magic

2026-27 record: 2-5
Previous ranking: 20
Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 5), @ GS (Nov. 7), @ SAC (Nov. 10)

No home-court identity. The two road wins against New York and Toronto proved that Orlando can compete with the top teams in the East. Playing at home is a different story. The Magic capped the second week of the regular season with home losses to Boston and Washington.

22. New Orleans Pelicans

2026-27 record: 3-4
Previous ranking: 26
Next games: vs. UTAH (Nov. 4), vs. MIN (Nov. 6), @ LAC (Nov. 8), @ GS (Nov. 9)

No Dejounte, no problem. Herbert Jones and Karlo Matkovic have added more size and versatility to the new-look starting lineup during the winning streak, leaving Mosley with some difficult decisions once Murray returns. -- Golliver

23. Indiana Pacers

2026-27 record: 2-6
Previous ranking: 11
Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 4), vs. DEN (Nov. 7), @ DAL (Nov. 9)

Injury bug bites again. It wasn't bad enough that Tyrese Haliburton is out for at least two weeks because of a hamstring injury. Indiana's entire starting five sat out Monday's game, albeit the second night of a back-to-back, giving the Pacers visions of last season when injuries to Haliburton started a wave throughout the roster.

Indiana will have to survive this early-season slog and hope for a throwback to two years ago. The Pacers were under .500 in mid-December before turning their season around in January with a run that carried them to the Finals. -- Jamal Collier

24. Phoenix Suns

2026-27 record: 1-4
Previous ranking: 19
Next games: vs. POR (Nov. 4), vs. ORL (Nov. 5), vs. HOU (Nov. 7), vs. SA (Nov. 9), vs. LAC (Nov. 10)

Both are contributing to the Suns ranking dead last in defensive rating, allowing 124 points per 100 possessions.

We knew the center position was a soft spot for this roster heading into the season, but it has been even worse than expected so far. -- McMenamin

25. LA Clippers

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 23
Next games: vs. MIA (Nov. 4), vs. NO (Nov. 8), @ PHX (Nov. 10)

Their offense has been hard to come by. Their leading scorer, Darius Garland, is averaging 20.1 points on 43.5% shooting, and their second-leading scorer, Rui Hachimura, is averaging 13.4 points on just 36.9% shooting. Maybe their next game against the Heat will be just what they need -- considering how rough the Heat's defense has been so far (27th in the league). -- McMenamin

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 21
Next games: @ NO (Nov. 4), @ DAL (Nov. 6), @ MIN (Nov. 8), vs. MIA (Nov. 10)

It doesn't help that Markkanen is now dealing with a sprained right (shooting) wrist as he attempts to establish a rhythm. -- MacMahon

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 25
Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 4), vs. PHI (Nov. 8)

Beginning of a rebuild. This is what step one of a rebuild looks like. The Bulls knew they had a long way to go when their new front office arrived this summer, and the start of the season has confirmed as much.

They have one win in their first seven games and haven't been super competitive against a tough schedule (they played Toronto with Kawhi Leonard, Boston twice, and will face the Knicks and Sixers for a second time later this week). Chicago ranks in the bottom five in both offensive and defensive efficiency and, outside of Caleb Wilson's strong start, not much has gone right so far. -- Collier

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 28
Next games: @ BOS (Nov. 4), vs. TOR (Nov. 6), vs. BOS (Nov. 8), @ NYK (Nov. 10)

Who survives the season? After trading their superstar over the summer, the Bucks have an ill-fitting roster that is clearly in transition. Milwaukee is looking for a new identity and the start of the season has not been encouraging with this many new players on the roster.

So, how will Milwaukee continue to remake its roster going forward? What does the future hold for some Bucks veterans, including Myles Turner, Kyle Kuzma and Tyler Herro, who are not on the same timeline as some of the Bucks' other young players, namely No. 10 pick Brayden Burries? -- Collier

2026-27 record: 1-6
Previous ranking: 29
Next games: vs. CHA (Nov. 4), @ ATL (Nov. 7), @ DAL (Nov. 8)

Playing with good intentions. That's about all you can say about the Nets at this point. They've held late leads, they've competed. At times, like Monday, Brooklyn gets a little scattered or too heavily dependent on Julius Randle to retrieve the team from the muck and it has a quicksand effect.

But on the positive side, the Nets rank No. 3 in the NBA with nearly 40% of their scoring coming from 3-point range, and No. 7 in makes at 14.3 per game. -- Goodwill

The rookie isn't shy. Here are Darius Acuff Jr.'s shot attempts in his first seven NBA games: 24, 26, 23, 20, 26, 25, 21. Everyone assumed the rebuilding Kings would give their 19-year-old point guard the ultimate green light. Acuff has accepted, slamming down the gas pedal. His first four games were inefficient. His past three have been encouraging -- 35-of-72 overall plus a 14-assist effort.

Acuff's most recent outing also led the previously 0-6 Kings to their first win. He had 25 points in Dallas and closed it out with a flurry, scoring seven in the last five minutes, including a dagger 3-pointer over Cooper Flagg. -- Slater

stories.headline: Harry Kane falls short of Cristiano Ronaldo Champions League goal streak record
stories.summary: Harry Kane failed to match Cristiano Ronaldo's record for scoring in the most consecutive Champions League games.
stories.body:
Harry Kane failed to match Cristiano Ronaldo's record for scoring in the most consecutive Champions League games.

Ronaldo's tally of scoring in 11 games in a row still stands after Kane, who had scored in 10 consecutive Champions League appearances, failed to get on the scoresheet on Tuesday against Atlético Madrid.

Bayern Munich beat Atletico 2-0 with goals from Lennart Karl and Konraid Laimer. The second strike came from a Kane assist.

Kane had scored for the 10th Champions League game in succession, and moved one behind the Madrid and Manchester United legend, on matchday three of the campaign with his penalty against Arsenal.

But fresh off claiming the Ballon d'Or, Kane missed out on matching Ronaldo's all-time tally despite helping Bayern win.

Ronaldo's total was set in 2017-18 as Madrid went on to win their third straight Champions League via a memorable victory over Liverpool in the final.

His 11-game run began with a brace against Juventus in the previous year's Champions League final. He then scored in all six group stage matches and in both legs of Madrid's round of 16 and quarterfinal ties.

- Kane says new Bayern deal 'extremely close,' will happen in coming days

Kane's 10-in-a-row run began when he scored twice against Union Saint-Gilloise on matchday seven of Bayern's 2025-26 Champions League campaign. He scored against PSV Eindhoven the following week before watching from the bench as his teammates beat Atalanta 6-1 in Italy in the first leg of their round of 16 meeting.

The former Tottenham Hotspur striker picked up where he left off with two goals in the second leg before finding the back of the net in every game as Bayern's hopes of European glory were ended by Paris Saint-Germain in the semifinals.

Kane has scored against Bodo/Glimt, Viking FK and Arsenal.

Who has scored in the most consecutive Champions League games?

11: Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid, 2017-18), Harry Kane (Bayern München, 2026-present)

9: Ruud van Nistelrooy (Manchester United, 2002-03)

As with any Wednesday, it's a lighter supply of NHL action this evening, but there are some fun matchups.

Ottawa Senators at Buffalo Sabres

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BUF -148, O/U: 6.5

Following playoff appearances by both of these Atlantic Division teams in 2026, the postseason seems a lot more likely for one than the other right now.

The Sens have started the season 9-6-1, and sit third in the division right now, though they have lost three of their last five. On the other side, the Sabres are 7-4-3, but bring a three-game winning streak into this contest.

This is the first game between the teams this season, and they'll play three additional games (Dec. 14, Feb. 26 and March 7). On the individual player front, keep an eye out for Ottawa's Tim Stutzle and Buffalo's Tage Thompson, who lead their respective clubs in scoring.

Chicago Blackhawks at Florida Panthers

7:30 p.m. ET (TNT) | FLA -250, O/U: 5.5

Given the relative positioning of these two teams in their competitive windows, it was a bit surprising to see the Panthers win by a narrow 3-2 margin on Oct. 25.

Wednesday's game will be the conclusion to the season series between the two teams; can the Blackhawks earn the upset?

Florida had the edge in the first matchup in shots (34-21), hits (33-18), faceoffs (53.6%) ... and penalty minutes (16-10). A better power play would serve the Blackhawks well in general -- they are currently 31st in the league, at 10.6% -- but will definitely aid in this coming matchup if they have a PIM edge again.

San Jose Sharks at Los Angeles Kings

10 p.m. ET (TNT) | LA -166, O/U: 6.5

These two squared off back on Oct. 3, with the Sharks earning a 5-4 overtime win thanks to the extra-time goal by Igor Chernyshov.

Both of these teams had some level of expectation that they'd make it to the playoffs this season. At some point, they'll need to start stringing together wins to get there. Scoring goals has been an issue for both, as the Kings are 25th in the league (2.77 goals per game) with the Sharks 27th (2.56).

Macklin Celebrini is again atop the Sharks' scoring sheet, with 16 points ahead of a pair at 10. Artemi Panarin leads the way for L.A. with 13 points, ahead of Brandt Clarke's 10.

Calgary Flames at Seattle Kraken

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | SEA -166, O/U: 6.5

While some divisional foes have yet to play a single game against one another, the Flames and Kraken are poised to play their fourth and final game on Wednesday.

Seattle won the first two games by 6-1 margins, while the Flames won Game 3 on Oct. 30 by a score of 6-2. So expect six goals for the winning team again?

Dustin Wolf has gotten the nod in goal for the Flames in each of the first three. Does that continue, or will it be the most interesting man in hockey, Devin Cooley, in Calgary's crease?

stories.headline: Brewers manager Pat Murphy says he regrets anti-Yankees comments to Jake Bauers
stories.summary: Brewers manager Pat Murphy says he regrets his recent comments to Jake Bauers about the Yankees, adding that he didn't intend to "slander" the Bronx Bombers.
stories.body:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy says he regrets his recent comments to Jake Bauers about the New York Yankees, adding that he didn't intend to "slander" the Bronx Bombers.

Murphy addressed his anti-Yankees barb with the New York Post's "The Show" podcast, which posted its interview with the Milwaukee manager Tuesday, six days after the Brewers won the first World Series title in franchise history.

As he celebrated with Bauers on the field after the Brewers' series-clinching Game 5 victory, Murphy mentioned "that horses--- Yankees team" where "you guys were all playing for yourself." The moment was captured on video and went viral last week.

Murphy told "The Show" that he contacted Brian Cashman and had a "good conversation" with the longtime Yankees general manager.

"I called Brian Cashman right away when I heard [my comments] got out," said Murphy, who added that he didn't realize he was "on a hot mic" during his exchange with Bauers.

"I tried to explain that I wasn't talking about the 2026 Yankees. I was just referring to the teams with a lot of money that sign a lot of players that sometimes end up not being that 'Little Engine that Could,' so to speak -- more of a high expectation, 'I gotta get mine.' I regret saying it."

Bauers, who played for the Yankees in 2023, caught the final out in Milwaukee's 4-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays. The brief conversation with Murphy started as the Brewers were celebrating on the field at Tropicana Field and Bauers presented Murphy with the ball from the series-clinching play.

"You're going to be a rich f---er," Murphy told Bauers, who is scheduled to become a free agent this offseason. "Just remember when you were on that horses--- Yankees team and you guys were all playing for yourself? Just remember, say, 'This is the way we used to do it.'"

Murphy told "The Show" that those remarks were consistent with the "rhetoric" he used with Bauers throughout Milwaukee's championship run.

"After every celebration, I'd shake his hand and I'd say, 'You rich so-and-so, you're going to leave us,'" Murphy said. "We're not going to be able to pay you. You're going to leave us, and you're going to forget all about how we did things. ... I would just give him this rhetoric every time."

Bauers enjoyed a breakout 2026 season, his third in Milwaukee since being traded to the Brewers by the Yankees in November 2023. He appeared in 84 games with New York that year, batting .202 with 12 home runs and 95 strikeouts in 272 plate appearances.

But Bauers has rejuvenated his career with the Brewers and posted career bests in virtually every offensive category in 2026, including batting average (.266), homers (26), RBIs (86) and OPS (.874). He was named MVP of Milwaukee's National League Championship Series victory over the Dodgers after batting .286 with six RBIs in the Brewers' four-game series sweep.

As for the Yankees, Murphy reiterated that he merely meant to reference a high-payroll team and that he was not singling them out.

"I felt horribly if I slandered the Yankees, because I was just kind of referring to them as this iconic machine. ... It wasn't smart on my part, and I'm sorry about it," he said.

stories.headline: 2027 WNBA championship odds: Lynx, Aces ahead of Dream, Valkyries
stories.summary: An early look at the odds to win the 2027 WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
After coming into the 2026 season as 45-1 underdogs to win the WNBA Finals, the Golden State Valkyries will be among the favorites to win the title in 2027, though there is little consensus across the sportsbook marketplace.

The Valkyries are the favorites to win the 2027 WNBA Finals at BetMGM, showing +300 odds ... but at DraftKings, the Minnesota Lynx -- who notched the 2026 regular season's best record -- are the favorites at +310, while Caesars Sportsbook and FanDuel have the Las Vegas Aces favored at +340 and +360, respectively. The 2026 runner-up Atlanta Dream are within the top four at all the sportsbooks, showing a short of +400 at DraftKings.

Just outside the top tier are Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever (+900 at DraftKings) and Paige Bueckers' Dallas Wings, who are a relatively long 14-1 at DraftKings, but are as short as +750 at BetMGM. There's also a wide range of odds on the New York Liberty, who are anywhere between +900 and 17-1 for the 2027 title after a relatively disappointing 2026 campaign that saw them come in as title favorites.

For all of the potential contenders at the top of the board, there is also a cadre of long shots at the bottom, with the Chicago Sky, Seattle Storm, Toronto Tempo and relocating Houston Comets all coming in at 120-1, per DraftKings lines.

Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up
stories.summary: Which teams are in the best position heading into Decision Day? All this and more in the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday and another weekend of action is in the books. With Decision Day coming up next week, it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings to see which teams are in a good or bad spot to qualify for the MLS Cup playoffs.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While seeking history on a rainy night in Tennessee, Nashville fell behind by two goals, had multiple goals called off, but battled back to force two own goals and clinch a 3-2 win against Red Bull New York with stoppage-time headed goal from Sam Surridge. The Supporters' Shield winners are level with Miami's points record, but could break it with just a point from their final game.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Miami reclaimed second place in the Eastern Conference with a second-half rally against the Revs to win 2-1, ignited by the guy still leading the Golden Boot race: Lionel Messi. After a headed assist to Germán Berterame to level the score, Messi scored his 26th goal of the year after finagling past multiple defenders then sending a low left-footed strike past Matt Turner.

3. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 4

The Revs' four-game win streak came to a halt against the Herons, as Messi proved the difference maker once more assisting and scoring in a come-from-behind win for Miami. With that, New England drops to third place in the Eastern Conference. Silver lining? Dániel Gazdag is now on a two-game scoring streak.

4. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

STL had the firepower in the attacking third to come away with all three points against San Diego. But thanks in part to Pablo Sisniega's six saves and Anders Dreyer's moment of quality, they went home with a 1-0 defeat instead. The playoffs were already locked up but home-field advantage isn't as they head into the final weekend.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

After going scoreless in six games, Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to make the difference in Colorado, providing the go-ahead goal 10 minutes after subbing on, then setting up Puso Dithejane for the 4-2 win.

6. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 7

The Whitecaps showed their quality in a comprehensive 5-1 dismantling of Seattle, highlighted by a Brian White brace that started in the 56th minute. After a 4-1 win over San Diego in midweek and 29th-place Montréal up next, the Western Conference's first-place side have got some momentum ahead of the postseason.

7. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

After drawing Nashville 0-0 in the midweek, Philly's 1-0 loss to Cincinnati is their second in three games. They'll be in the postseason, but they may have a tough matchup when it comes.

8. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 9

With the Golden Boot technically still in reach, Petar Musa (who scored 22 goals this season) missed his first penalty in six this season in the 97th minute. Stefan Cleveland's late-game save kept the Toros from three points in a 1-1 draw as they head into the final weekend looking to secure second place in the Western Conference.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

After losing 3-1 to Minnesota, LAFC are winless in three (two draws) ahead of a Decision Day battle with the Sounders. With their playoff place secure, they're competing for a better finish in the standings, but will fall short of their top-three finish in the Western Conference in the last four seasons.

10. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Kristijan Kahlina, whose save percentage (75.9%) is second only to first-place Nashville's Brian Schwake (77.7%), stopped eight against Orlando in a match that ended 4-0 in Charlotte's favor, despite both teams firing off the same number of shots (and nearly the same on target, though Charlotte had higher quality opportunities).

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 11

After losing 4-0 to mid-table side Charlotte, Orlando picked up their first defeat in six games but still clinched their playoff spot based on other results. They're in the final wild card spot ahead of a final test against the Revs.

12. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

The Quakes took 17 minutes to score twice against RSL, and that was enough to secure three points in a 2-1 win. That's their first win in six (four draws, one loss) as they look to secure their third-place spot in the Western Conference.

13. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

In a 5-1 loss to Vancouver, Jordan Morris' brief light of life in the second half was overshadowed by the Whitecaps' rapid response in a match characterized by goalkeeper Andy Thomas looking painfully skyward for help from the scoreline. After losing to Houston in midweek, the Sounders have three defeats and no wins from their last five games. They play LAFC on the final day while sitting one place short of the wild card spots.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 14

Morgan Whittaker scored from close range to mark his third goal in three games and take an early 1-0 lead against Chicago. But at the end of a goal-heavy matchup, Lewandowski scored and assisted off the bench to help see the Fire to a 4-2 win. The Rapids ended the weekend in the final playoff position and have a tough final test against Dallas to hang on.

15. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 17

Cincinnati only forced one save out of Andre Blake, but with the help of Roman Celentano's six stops, they booked their playoff spot with a 1-0 win against the Union. Ayoub Jabbari came off the bench in the second half and registered the sole tally of the night, capitalizing on Blake's save (a low-struck ball from Evander) to score off the rebound.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 16

The Dynamo could secure home advantage in the playoffs with a top-of-the-table finish, but are hanging on to fifth place ahead of the final day after losing 3-1 to Portland (their first loss in six). They have a decisive meeting with St. Louis on the final day, who are just ahead of them on goal difference but tied on points.

17. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 19

Sergi Roberto's first MLS goal was the icing on the cake of a 4-1 win against Austin that also featured Hirving Lozano's first goal back from injury and three assists from Marco Reus. Austin's not the toughest opponent in MLS this season, but the result matters as the Galaxy head into the final weekend still competing for a playoff spot.

18. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 20

The Crew may have lost the U.S. Open Cup final, but after beating D.C United 3-0, they're finishing the regular season on a five-game win streak. They confirmed their spot in the postseason and finished the weekend in one of the Eastern Conference's two wild card positions.

19. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 22

The Timbers secured a massive three points in a 3-1 win against the Dynamo highlighted by two assists and a goal from Vincent Janssen (nearly half his total goal contributions this year). With one game remaining, they're in a wild card spot and have one tentative hand on the playoffs.

20. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 23

In his first start since September, Joaquín Pereyra powered the Loons to three points with two goals against LAFC in a 3-1 win. They're still short of a final playoff spot (by two points) but following this result, they can still potentially break in with a win (and other results going in their favor), with San Jose waiting on the final day.

21. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

After falling behind 2-0 early to San Jose, Juan Manuel Sanabria's headed goal (his second of the year) in the 23rd minute provided life, but unfortunately nothing followed. They're currently outside the wild card spots ahead of a crucial final game against the Galaxy, but will also need some results to go their way.

22. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 12

RBNY had an early penalty stopped but came out with the upper hand against Nashville, taking a 2-0 lead in Tennessee that started with a beautiful link up between league wonderkids Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall. But after two own goals and a stoppage-time winner from Nashville, the Red Bulls were eliminated from the playoffs in consecutive seasons for the first time ever.

23. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 21

After conceding a 91st-minute goal to last-placed Montréal, the Pigeons' playoff chances are officially over. A 1-1 draw isn't enough to launch them into the wild card position with one more game to go.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 26

Dreyer -- a back-to-back MLS All-Star -- won't feature in this year's postseason, but that didn't stop him from handing the recently-crowded U.S. Open Cup champions a loss in a 1-0 victory over St. Louis. Dreyer's left-footed chip from distance was a taste of quality we'll be missing seven days from now.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 24

With no postseason hopes, victories must come from small achievements, like letting Reus assist three goals or having a goalkeeper make six saves while still conceding four.

26. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

Toronto succumbed to a 3-1 defeat to Atlanta and ended their postseason dream in the process. Back to the drawing board for Robin Fraser's side, who showed signs of potential earlier in the season.

27. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 28

With the playoffs out of the picture and the all-time goals conceded in a single season record newly secured, SKC still did their best to sabotage Dallas by absconding with a 1-1 draw against a side looking to lock up their top-two finish in the Western Conference.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 29

Miguel Almirón won't appear in this year's playoffs, so he put on an end-of-season show in a 3-1 win against Toronto while eliminating the fellow Eastern Conference team from the playoffs. Five Stripes fans will take what they can get this year.

29. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

After losing to Toronto in the midweek, D.C. played Columbus with the playoffs already out of the picture and proceeded to lose 3-0. With 11 years since their last postseason victory, there's nowhere to go but up for this MLS original.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

It's too late to save their season, but not too late to sink somebody else's. A 91st-minute response to NYCFC's 1-0 lead secured their 26th point of the year and put to rest New York's postseason dream.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli is F1 champion. But why didn't he get his trophy in Mexico City?
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli is F1 world champion, but he won't get his trophy until December. Why does the sport still deny its champions their crowning moment?
stories.body:
There was one rather significant thing missing from Kimi Antonelli's world championship celebrations in Mexico City: the world championship trophy itself.

Despite becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history, the Italian will have to wait until Dec. 12 to get his hands on the prize he has spent his life chasing. That is because, unlike almost every other major sporting competition, F1 does not hand its championship trophy to the winner at the moment of victory. Instead, Antonelli will receive it while wearing a tuxedo, in a sterile hall, at the FIA's annual prize-giving gala dinner in Shanghai in December, six weeks after clinching the title.

It is one of F1's more peculiar traditions, denying the sport the sort of iconic sporting image synonymous with its biggest prizes. Think of the World Cup, the Super Bowl's Vince Lombardi Trophy or NHL's Stanley Cup, just to name three. The moment of triumph and the presentation of the trophy are inseparable. It doesn't have to be a conventional trophy, either. The Masters has turned the previous winner presenting the new winner a green blazer one of the most iconic images in all of sports.

F1's championship trophy, by contrast, seems almost an afterthought. Many fans would struggle to recognise it, which seems crazy for the series which is the pinnacle of motor racing.

It is a shame, too, because it is an impressive piece of silverware. Introduced in 1995, the trophy is made of sterling silver with gold detailing and features the signatures of Formula 1's world champions, stretching back to Giuseppe Farina in 1950.

So why wasn't it visible in Mexico City?

The answer lies in the divide between Formula 1 and its governing body, the FIA.

While F1, owned by Liberty Media, controls the commercial side of the championship, the FIA oversees its sporting and regulatory affairs. The world championship trophy falls under the FIA's jurisdiction -- Antonelli on Sunday officially became the FIA Formula 1 world champion - and its regulations stipulate that it must be presented at the governing body's annual gala.

Liberty Media has been keen to make more of the championship trophy. Sources have told ESPN discussions over a change this year did take place -- as they have for successive years now -- that the trophy be presented to Antonelli the moment he won it this year. However, as has also happened in previous seasons, it was agreed the FIA would stick with the convention of previous seasons and opt against doing anything radically different this time around.

- Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest world champion with maiden title

- Verstappen wins Mexico City GP for Red Bull; Antonelli seals historic title

- Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

The FIA has long argued that presenting the trophy at its gala is important to the occasion's prestige. The event celebrates champions from across motorsport, including rallying, endurance racing and karting, with the presence of Formula 1's world champion regarded as an important attraction for the younger winners.

There is also a sporting justification, as race results can be challenged or altered after the chequered flag, potentially changing the outcome of a championship. The FIA prefers to wait until those matters are settled before handing over its biggest prize.

That argument has some merit, although less so when Antonelli has wrapped up the championship with four races still to run. It rather falls apart altogether when considering what happens at every grand prix as it is the exact opposite of the practice the FIA puts forward in that instance. Individual race trophies are handed out immediately after the finish, despite those results also being subject to protests, penalties and subsequent disqualifications. If a result changes, the trophies simply change hands.

Look no further than Sunday's race in Mexico City for an example. Antonelli was clutching his third-place Mexico City Grand Prix trophy in his hands at different points during his celebratory moments on the podium and the ceremony which followed. That despite the fact a post-race penalty or protest could have moved him down the order after the fact -- it wouldn't have stopped him being champion, but it would have meant he should not have been on the podium. And yet, he did not have the world championship trophy in his hand for that exact same reason.

There is little reason why the championship should be treated differently to an individual race, especially when the current practice stops the trophy becoming a prize that champions can share with fans in the celebratory moments.

It seems a missed opportunity for a sport which has spent the past decade transforming the way it presents itself to the world. F1 has embraced new audiences, new technology and new ways of celebrating its biggest moments, yet its most prestigious prize remains tied to an awards dinner.

Antonelli will undoubtedly enjoy getting his hands on the trophy in Shanghai. But the moment he became world champion, surrounded by his Mercedes team and thousands of celebrating fans in Mexico City, has already passed and it is a moment Formula 1 cannot recreate.

stories.headline: AFL 2027 fixture: Five must-watch games in the first month
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month.
stories.body:
The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month of action.

Get the popcorn ready and get set to enjoy these absolute belters in the new year.

5. Port Adelaide vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 4, Adelaide Oval, Sunday, April 8, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Make no mistake, when Zak Butters returns to Adelaide Oval to face his old mob for the first time since departing, it's going to be incredibly spicy.

In a move that shocked absolutely nobody, Butters left Port Adelaide during the 2026 trade period, inking a long-term deal with the Western Bulldogs. It's a brutal blow for the Power, and his ex-teammates will be sure to give him a hard time when they share the field in Round 4. You just know it's going to be on for young and old!

The AFL also made the move to schedule this blockbuster game as the closer to next year's Gather Round. It means far more bodies will be in Adelaide that weekend and a greater number of eyeballs on the clash.

4. Hawthorn vs. Geelong - Round 2, MCG, Monday, March 29, 3:15pm (AEDT)
The traditional Easter Monday clash between the Hawks and Cats is always on our shortlist of early season must-watch games, and next year will be no exception.

Both of these clubs are in the premiership window. Both clubs have added high-profile players this offseason. Both clubs have fanbases that bring an electric energy to Easter Monday at the MCG.

This one is also set to be a fascinating coaching battle between Chris Scott and Sam Mitchell, two of the game's best tacticians, who will go head-to-head just as much as the players on the field.

3. Fremantle vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 1, Optus Stadium, Thursday, March 18, 8:10pm (AEDT)
This Round 1 game in the west is simply oozing with intrigue.

Of course, the question on everyone's mind is how the Dockers back up after having this year's premiership ripped away from them in harrowing circumstances. Does it galvanise the club? Will we see 'Wharfie Time'? Surely not!

For the Bulldogs, they landed the biggest fish of the off-season in superstar midfielder Zak Butters. This will be the first opportunity to watch him play in his new colours, lining up in the middle alongside skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards.

2. Brisbane vs. Collingwood - Round 2, Gabba, Thursday, March 25, 7:50pm (AEDT)
Reigning premier Brisbane will unfurl its latest flag in Round 2 when it hosts Collingwood in its first home game of the season, a clash that has blockbuster written all over it.

The Lions are looking to become just the second team ever to win four consecutive flags (joining, you guessed it, Collingwood from 1927 to 1930) but will be doing it without superstar midfielder Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow medallist departed for the Magpies this offseason, making this early season contest between the two clubs extra intriguing.

Plus, any opportunity to watch current Brownlow medallist Nick Daicos play footy is reason in itself to tune in!

1. Hawthorn vs. Brisbane - Round 1, MCG, Friday, March 19, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Thankfully we don't have to wait long for the Hawks and Lions -- quite possibly the competition's two best teams -- to square off in 2027. And if this game delivers even 70% of what these sides dished up in this year's epic preliminary final, then we're in for an absolute treat!

Many have labelled Brisbane's thrilling win over Hawthorn this past September as the greatest game of footy played this century. That in itself should be enough of a reason for their next clash to simply be must-watch.

There will be extra intrigue with both teams given this clash falls in Round 1. For the Lions, they will be looking to navigate life without both superstar midfielder Lachie Neale and master coach Chris Fagan, while the Hawks will be attempting to integrate recruits Zach Merrett and Ben King into their line-up.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Cowboys keen on Raiders' Savage
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news on Bradman Best's future and which clubs might be lining up a play for Sam Walker.
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Cowboys among clubs eyeing Savage

North Queensland are among the clubs showing interest in Canberra winger Xavier Savage, as rivals assess their recruitment options for 2028.

ESPN understands the Cowboys and a Sydney-based club are keeping tabs on the speedster, who is contracted to the Raiders until the end of 2027 and became eligible to negotiate with rivals on November 1.

Savage scored 13 tries in 19 NRL appearances for Canberra this season.

Bryenton begins Tigers chapter

David Bryenton will begin full-time training with the Wests Tigers on Wednesday, with ESPN understanding the recruit features in Benji Marshall's long-term plans.

Having first reported his signing last month, ESPN can reveal Bryenton's mutually agreed release from the Bulldogs has now been finalised, clearing the way for him to join Marshall's squad for pre-season.

Dolphins win race for Su'a

The Dolphins have won the race to retain Sebastian Su'a, with ESPN understanding the young forward has agreed to terms on a two-year extension that will keep him in Redcliffe until the end of 2029.

Several NRL clubs had identified Su'a as a potential recruitment target, but the Dolphins have moved to secure his future with the club.

Fa'alogo agrees to long-term Storm extension

Sua Fa'alogo has agreed to extend his stay at the Melbourne Storm through to the end of 2032, ESPN understands.

The agreement will keep the fullback in Melbourne for the next six seasons, securing a key figure in the Storm's long-term plans.

Fa'alogo's retention delivers a major boost for Melbourne ahead of the November 1 contracting window, with the club moving to lock down one of its most exciting talents.

Dolphins close in on Lemuelu extension, confident of keeping Farnworth

The Dolphins are closing in on a multi-year extension for Connelly Lemuelu as they also express confidence in retaining Herbie Farnworth.

ESPN understands Lemuelu is nearing an agreement to extend his stay despite interest from Canberra, Parramatta and Cronulla.

Securing the back-rower would deliver a retention boost for the Dolphins, with the length of the proposed deal yet to be confirmed.

The club is also understood to be confident it can retain Farnworth despite links to the Sydney Roosters.

While that confidence is yet to translate into a confirmed extension, keeping the English international alongside Lemuelu would help preserve key combinations on the Dolphins' left edge.

Eels edge ahead in Best race
Parramatta have emerged as the frontrunners to land Bradman Best, with multiple sources indicating the Newcastle centre is increasingly likely to join the Eels beyond 2027.

Best has been identified as a priority target for Parramatta, who are looking to bolster Jason Ryles' backline with an established representative star.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the Eels are understood to be in the box seat despite Newcastle's efforts to retain him with a lucrative extension.

Bulldogs unlikely to enter Walker race
Canterbury are unlikely to enter the race for Sam Walker, with the Bulldogs backing their existing halfback options ahead of the upcoming season.

Despite suggestions the club could emerge as a potential destination for Walker, it is understood Canterbury are taking a wait-and-see approach rather than preparing to launch a pursuit.

The Bulldogs' immediate focus remains on the internal battle for the No.7 jersey, with Mitch and Alex Conti set to compete for the role over the offseason.

Canterbury have not completely shut the door on a move should circumstances change, but their current position suggests they are unlikely to become an active contender for Walker's signature.

For now, the Bulldogs are content to watch how the situation unfolds.
